claim: Going first limits only Turn-1 Energy and attacks: across 25 clips that player still played Items (Poke Ball), Supporters (Professor's Research, Copycat, Team Rocket's Master Plan, Lisia), Tools (Sitrus Berry, Heavy Helmet, Giant Cape), a Stadium (Soothing Shore), and benched up to three Basics.

result.evidence: The only first-player-specific limit in the engine is the Energy Zone. Turn 1 starts with no rotation (engine/src/actions/apply_action_helpers.rs:72-76, comment 'no energy generation'); setup only pre-fills `next` (engine/src/state/mod.rs:768-772); a manual Attach is offered only when `current` is Some (engine/src/move_generation/mod.rs:77-92). Nothing else checks the turn. generate_possible_trainer_actions blocks Trainers only at turn_count==0 (setup), then applies the normal one-Supporter and Item-lock checks (engine/src/move_generation/move_generation_trainer.rs:52-67; hooks/core.rs:657-685). The cards named are unconditional or need only a non-empty deck: Poke Ball :564-570, Professor's Research :550-559, Copycat :239, Lisia :251-253, Team Rocket's Master Plan :336-338, Clemont's Backpack :261. Tools need only a legal target (:387-396; Giant Cape, Heavy Helmet and Sitrus Berry are implemented, tools.rs:138-166). Stadiums need only 'none played this turn / different name / no Massive Body' (:399-428; Soothing Shore implemented, stadiums.rs:75). Basics go to any empty slot of the 3-slot Bench (move_generation/mod.rs:176-186; state/mod.rs:314). Test: engine/tests/trainers/cynthia_test.rs:13-30 generates a Supporter as a legal action at turn_count=1. The T1 state is pinned by apply_actions_test.rs:228-249 (first player has no current Energy) and :202-206 (no Attach offered).
result.note: Two nuances in the wording. (1) Attacks are not banned on Turn 1. They are limited only by cost, so a 0-cost attack is offered (see S4). (2) The no-evolution rule is not a going-first limit: it covers both players' first turns (move_generation/mod.rs:209, is_users_first_turn = turn_count<=2 at state/mod.rs:1227-1229). Rare Candy is blocked on turn 1 (move_generation_trainer.rs:663-666, matching its printed text). Cyrus can't be played by the first player on T1 because no opposing Benched Pokémon can have damage yet (:637-648). Both appear in the card list. If any clip actually showed either one played on the first player's T1, that would be a contradiction, but the claim doesn't say so.

claim: The player going first still draws a card at the start of Turn 1, reported across 11 clips; named draws include Eevee (~44s), Field Blower and Soothing Shore.

result.evidence: At the start of turn 1 the engine queues a 1-card draw for the first player: engine/src/actions/apply_action_helpers.rs:73-76 (turn_count=1, then queue_draw_action(current_player,1)). The draw resolves through maybe_draw_card, which respects the 10-card hand limit and an empty deck (state/mod.rs:811-831). Test: engine/tests/engine/apply_actions_test.rs:10-35 (test_initial_build_phase). After setup plus the T1 draw, the first player's deck is 14 and the second player's is 15 (lines 32-34), so the first player has drawn 5+1. state/mod.rs:1571-1582 confirms both players are dealt 5 (decks at 15) before that draw.
result.note: This matches rules/01 §3 and RULES_FOR_AGENTS.md:38-39 (the first player does draw; Game8 EN is wrong). On ordering: at the turn-1 start, a start-of-turn Ability such as Meloetta's Strange Singing runs inside the same mutation, just before the draw is queued (apply_action_helpers.rs:75-76). No claim here tests that order.

claim: Two packets report Energy on the going-first player's Active on Turn 1, against the no-Energy rule: Pikachu got 1 Lightning (seen, not re-checked by the lead) and Riolu showed 1 Fighting in an inferred Turn-1 window (flagged review_needed). Neither attacked.

result.evidence: In the engine, the player going first can't get Zone Energy onto a Pokémon on Turn 1 except through a card effect. There is no rotation at the turn-1 start (engine/src/actions/apply_action_helpers.rs:72-76). energy_zone.current stays None (state/mod.rs:768-772; test apply_actions_test.rs:228-249, 'Player going first must NOT have an attachable energy on turn 1'). Attach is generated only from `current` (move_generation/mod.rs:77-92; test apply_actions_test.rs:202-206). A Pikachu (Gnaw, 1 Lightning, per lib/card.py) or a Riolu with 1 Energy on the first player's T1 is therefore impossible in the engine unless a card effect put it there. Examples: Electric Generator, which attaches only to a Benched [L] Pokémon, or Zeraora's end-of-first-turn Thunderclap Flash (hooks/core.rs:521-551). The claim names no such effect.
result.note: WEAK contradiction. Do not change the engine on this basis. The engine follows the OFFICIAL in-app Tips ('On the first turn of the player who goes first, no Energy will be generated'), and the first pass's R243 had several 'seen' clips showing no T1 Energy. One report is 'seen, not re-checked'. The other rests on an inferred T1 window marked 'unclear'/review_needed. The likely explanations are a misread turn or seat, or an Energy from a card effect. What would settle it: re-check 20260907_031901 00:13-00:25 for the 'Current turn' banner, whose Pikachu it is, whether that player was going first, and any Trainer or Ability that attached Energy. For SweetGameBuddy 00:24-00:33, check who went first and whose turn it was. This same pass cites 00:48-01:00 of that video as the second player's T2, so the Riolu's window and owner need confirming.

claim: The player going first attacked on Turn 1 in two battles: Igglybuff's Sleepy Lullaby (no Energy cost, 10 plus Sleep, Sleep Checkup at end of T1) was seen; an unverified outline has Happiny's Chubby Cheer for 10 after Professor's Research (Ogerpon ex 130 to 120).

result.evidence: The engine has no turn-1 attack ban. generate_attack_actions gates only on status, effects and cost (engine/src/move_generation/attacks.rs:14-80). An empty cost always passes (hooks/core.rs:2099-2135: energy_missing of [] is empty). The comment 'only starting on turn 2' at move_generation/mod.rs:110 is stale. Igglybuff A4a 059 has energy_required: vec![] and Sleepy Lullaby 10 (database.rs:34612-34617), mapped to InflictStatusConditions Asleep (effect_mechanic_map.rs:2371-2375). Happiny's Chubby Cheer is 0-cost 10 (lib/card.py), mapped to IncreasedDamageNextTurn +20 (effect_mechanic_map.rs:2523-2527). Professor's Research doesn't end the turn and is playable on T1 (move_generation_trainer.rs:550-559). Any non-setup EndTurn, turn 1 included, runs end-of-turn effects and then Pokémon Checkup (apply_action_helpers.rs:81-83 -> 87-117), so the Sleep flip happens at the end of T1. Test: cynthia_test.rs:13-38 generates an Attack as a legal action at turn_count=1 (Energy supplied by the fixture). The first pass's R238 checked the Sleepy Lullaby -> Bad Dreams -> Checkup order on this clip (190933 ~70-86s).
result.note: No test asserts that a specifically 0-cost attack is offered on T1. The code path is clear, though, and the claim agrees with RULES_FOR_AGENTS.md:39-41 and the official FAQ. The Happiny half is 'inferred' only (012720), but the engine would allow it: Ogerpon ex 130 -> 120, and Happiny is Colorless, so no Weakness.

claim: The player going second gets a full first turn (Turn 2): it draws, attaches Energy and may attack, across 13 clips (Fire attach then Peck for 20, Electrike 60 to 40; Moltres ex attached Fire and used Inferno Dance; Jab for 20, Heatmor 80 to 60).

result.evidence: When the first player ends turn 1, advance_turn switches player, sets turn_count 2, queues a 1-card draw and rotates the new player's Energy Zone, so `next` becomes `current` (engine/src/state/mod.rs:1199-1207, 931-939). Attach is then offered (move_generation/mod.rs:77-92). Attacks have no turn gate (move_generation/attacks.rs:14-80). Test: engine/tests/engine/apply_actions_test.rs:253-280 (after the first player's EndTurn: turn_count==2, current_player==second player, current Energy == the previewed next). The examples fit the card texts from lib/card.py and the engine: Torchic Peck [R] 20 (Electrike 60 -> 40), Riolu A2 091 Jab [F] 20 (Heatmor 80 -> 60, Heatmor weak to Water), and Moltres ex Inferno Dance [R] after a manual Fire attach.
result.note: 'Full' first turn still excludes evolution. The engine blocks evolving on T2 as well (move_generation/mod.rs:209; state/mod.rs:1227-1229), matching the official rule. The one exception is the Active Eevee's Boosted Evolution (move_generation/mod.rs:198-218; test additional_ability_logic_test.rs:149-166), which covers a T2 Eevee -> Jolteon ex (232035). The card list also names Swablu and Mega Altaria ex. If a clip showed Swablu -> Mega Altaria ex on the second player's T2, the engine would contradict it, but the claim doesn't say that happened.

claim: One turn counter covers both players: the player going first takes the odd-numbered turns (1, 3, 5...) and the player going second the even ones (2, 4, 6...); one match ended on turn 14.

result.evidence: turn_count is one global counter ('Global turn count. Matches TCGPocket app.', engine/src/state/mod.rs:284). The first player starts at 1 (apply_action_helpers.rs:69-73). Each advance_turn flips the player and adds 1 (state/mod.rs:1199-1200), so the first player gets the odd turns and the second the even ones. Tests: apply_actions_test.rs:228-233 (turn 1 = first player) and :253-273 (turn 2 = second player). Turn limit: turn_count>30 -> Tie (state/mod.rs:1201-1204; test state/mod.rs:1693-1705), so ending on turn 14 is ordinary.
result.note: `current_player` can briefly point at the other player for a forced choice (comment at state/mod.rs:289-291, 'see Sabrina'). Turn ownership still follows turn_count parity.

claim: Each turn starts with an automatic draw: the second player drew at the start of T2, and a Copycat drawn at the start of T6 was played that same turn.

result.evidence: Every turn from 2 on starts with queue_draw_action(current_player, 1) in advance_turn (engine/src/state/mod.rs:1206), subject to the 10-card limit and empty-deck rules (state/mod.rs:811-831; test :1677-1691). Turn 1 does the same (apply_action_helpers.rs:76). Nothing stops a card drawn this turn from being played: hand actions come straight from the current hand (move_generation/mod.rs:169-231). Copycat is unconditional (move_generation_trainer.rs:239) and limited only by the one-Supporter rule (hooks/core.rs:657-676). Test of the start-of-turn draw on a later turn: engine/tests/pokemon/additional_ability_logic_test.rs:168-195. After the opponent's EndTurn, player 0's hand is 2 cards from a 2-card deck: the automatic draw plus Meloetta's search.
result.note: Ordering detail, not asked here: for turns 2+, the engine rotates the Energy Zone immediately (state/mod.rs:1207), while the queued draw resolves on the next tick. The in-app Tips say draw first, then generate Energy. Both are independent random events, so the difference can't be observed.

claim: Turn order is set by an opening coin flip, shown as an animation and followed by a banner such as 'You are going second'; in one battle the player who won the opening coin went first.

result.evidence: State::initialize flips a fair coin for the starting player: `state.current_player = rng.gen_range(0..2)` (engine/src/state/mod.rs:765-766). That player sets up first, the turn passes to the other for their setup (apply_action_helpers.rs:52-60), and after the second setup EndTurn the turn returns to the coin winner at turn_count=1 (apply_action_helpers.rs:63-73). The coin winner always goes first, and neither player can choose to go second. Test: engine/tests/setup_information_test.rs:52-77 (for either first seat, turn 1 starts with current_player == the player who set up first).
result.note: The animation and the 'You are going first/second' banner are UI and not modeled. The engine deals the 5-card hands before the flip (state/mod.rs:758-766). The game flips first. The flip is independent of the deal, so the outcome distributions are the same.

claim: During setup a player places an Active and may also Bench Basics before Turn 1 (a second Greavard; Ekans and Koffing behind Magmar), or leave the Bench empty (a lone Eevee; a lone Nacli).

result.evidence: In setup (turn_count==0) the engine offers only Place(_,0) until an Active is down. After that it offers Place for each empty Bench slot (up to 3) plus EndTurn, so leaving the Bench empty is legal (engine/src/move_generation/mod.rs:30-42, 140-167). Only stage-0 Pokémon can be placed (mod.rs:176-186). Trainers, Fossils included, can't be played in setup (move_generation_trainer.rs:52-53). Test: engine/tests/setup_information_test.rs:52-77. Each player places a single Basic and ends setup with an empty Bench, and turn 1 starts normally.
result.note: The engine requires the Active before any Bench placement, while the real game lets you place in any order before Start Battle. The resulting boards are the same. No test places Bench Basics during setup specifically. That rests on the code path above.

claim: The opening hand is 5 cards: seen in one battle, and inferred in another (4 cards left after placing a lone Eevee, 5 after the first-turn draw). After Setup no Energy is attached and the score is 0-0.

result.evidence: Each player is dealt 5 (engine/src/state/mod.rs:761-764) after the swap-in shuffle: 5 random cards, with one swapped for a Basic only if none is Basic (deck.rs:129-149). Tests: state/mod.rs:1571-1582 (hands 5/5, decks 15/15, each with a Basic) and deck.rs:223-237. Placing a Basic removes it from the hand, and the next draw adds 1, giving 4 then 5. Points start at [0,0] (state/mod.rs:535). Setup attaches no Energy: at the turn-1 start neither Zone has a current Energy (test state/mod.rs:1623-1640), and the Active has no Energy right after initialization (apply_actions_test.rs:194-200).
result.note: The 5-card hand is 'seen' in one clip and 'inferred' in the other. Either way the engine agrees, and so does the settled opening-hand rule (rules/05 #6, RULES_FOR_AGENTS.md:35-37).

claim: During setup (Set Active Pokemon), the opponent's chosen Active stays face-down and is revealed only at the 'Ready? Go!' start: the opposing Riolu was hidden at 00:18 and shown at 00:24.

result.evidence: While turn_count==0, PlayerObservation hides the opponent's whole board (`template.in_play_pokemon[opponent].fill(None)` with setup_opponent_hidden=true), and the actual board is kept (engine/src/observation.rs:48-53). Once the second setup EndTurn sets turn_count=1, both boards are visible. Tests: engine/tests/independent_setup_visibility_test.rs:43-50 (the second setter's observation is identical whether the hidden opponent Active is Bulbasaur or Charmander). engine/tests/setup_information_test.rs:52-77 checks that the opponent's board stays hidden after each setup step and is fully revealed to both viewers at turn 1. setup_information_test.rs:41-51 covers the Bench as well.
result.note: The engine runs setup one player after the other rather than at the same time, but the observation mask gives the same information as the game's face-down placement. The 'Ready? Go!' reveal animation is UI only.

claim: Poke Ball's search includes Basic Pokemon ex (Entei ex; Skarmory ex in several battles; Indeedee ex on T13). The found Basic went to hand, not the Bench; benching was a separate action (Lillipup benched on T1, left in hand on T7).

result.evidence: Both Poké Ball printings go to pokemon_search_outcomes(acting_player, state, true) (engine/src/actions/apply_trainer_action.rs:99-101). The filter is card.is_basic() (engine/src/actions/shared_mutations.rs:21-27), and is_basic means stage == 0 (engine/src/models/card.rs:243-248). Basic ex cards are stage 0 in engine/database.json: Entei ex A4a 010, Skarmory ex A4 124 and Indeedee ex B1 121 all read stage=0. The chosen card goes to the hand through transfer_card_from_deck_to_hand, and then the deck is shuffled (shared_mutations.rs:170-178; state/mod.rs:833-842). Benching is a separate Place action. Tests: engine/tests/s189_hidden_zone_eligibility.rs:64-88 (Poké Ball puts Bulbasaur in the hand: hand == [A1 001], deck 3->2, Poké Ball discarded) and engine/tests/engine/apply_actions_test.rs:116-145 (hand size unchanged, i.e. 'filled with basic', deck -1). No test uses an ex target, so the ex part rests on the stage==0 code path.
result.note: Unrelated to the claim but found while checking: the A2b 111 Poké Ball printing is in the 'always can play' list (move_generation_trainer.rs:214). Only P-A 005 has the empty-deck block (move_generation_trainer.rs:140, 561-570, commented 'deliberately limited to the measured print'). rules/04:84 says Poké Ball with an empty deck is blocked, so A2b 111 can be played with an empty deck. It does not appear in the known-deviation lists.

claim: An opponent's Poke Ball result is hidden from the other player: a face-down card moved from deck to hand, the deck shuffled, and the found Basic was never named; one stayed unidentified though Riolu was benched later. The owner's own fetches (Darkrai ex, Absol) showed on the owner's screen.

result.evidence: Every bot decides from PlayerObservation (engine/src/game.rs:224-232). It replaces the opponent's hand and deck with Card::Unknown and keeps the count (engine/src/observation.rs:56-57), so a Basic arriving from Poké Ball is seen as one more card back. Any remembered opponent-hand knowledge is cleared when that hand changes (observation.rs:678-683). Poké Ball's search makes no reveal event (shared_mutations.rs:170-178). The only public_reveal_events push is an attack's deck-prefix reveal (apply_attack_action.rs:5474-5481). The deck is shuffled after the search (shared_mutations.rs:177). The owner's own hand is not masked, so the owner sees its own fetch (Darkrai ex, Absol). Test: observation.rs:1218-1229 (the opponent's hidden hand slots are sampled, sizes are unchanged, and the observer's own hand equals the real hand). This agrees with rules/04_actions_cards_effects.md:148-149 (seen x3 plus Dustin's general rule).
result.note: This conflicts with S14 (same area, second pass).

claim: Poke Ball's result is not consistently hidden or shown: in two battles every Poke Ball, the opponent's included, showed the found Basic publicly, and another opponent's revealed Team Rocket's Slowpoke (owner's own revealed Oricorio), while a different opponent's T3 Poke Ball never revealed its card.

result.evidence: The engine never shows an opponent's Poké Ball result. It resolves to a hidden card in PlayerObservation (observation.rs:56, 678-683), and pokemon_search_outcomes creates no reveal event (shared_mutations.rs:16-28, 137-182). So the claim that it is sometimes shown publicly (opponent's Entei ex in 023151 T2, Growlithe in 155818 T16, Team Rocket's Slowpoke in 221914 T2) is not modelled. The owner seeing its own Oricorio is not a difference, because the engine also shows the owner its own hand.
result.note: This is a weak contradiction. It conflicts with S13 and with rules/04:148-149 (face-down fetch seen frame by frame x3, plus Dustin's rule that any deck-to-hand card is hidden). In each claimed public case the Basic was benched right after the Poké Ball. rules/04:148 flagged that exact pattern in 220914 as the reviewer reading back from the bench play. The 155818 review itself says the opponent's T2 Poké Ball result could not be assigned (REVIEW.md line 49), yet it calls T16 'visibly finds Growlithe'. To settle it: step frame by frame through 221914 00:32-00:52, 023151 T2 (~99s) and 155818 T16 (~05:10-05:23), and check whether a face-up card appears before any Bench placement.

claim: Copycat shuffles the user's hand into the deck (not the discard), then draws a variable count, not a fixed 3: 4 when the opponent held 4 cards (user had 1 left); elsewhere 4, 4, 4 and 5 with the opponent's hand size not shown.

result.evidence: copycat_effect (engine/src/actions/apply_trainer_action.rs:2176-2197) does three things in order. It counts the opponent's hand size (2182). It appends the whole hand to the deck, not the discard, and shuffles (2190-2191). It then calls maybe_draw_card once per opponent card (2194-2196). Copycat itself has already been discarded by the play prefix, so it is not shuffled in (apply_action_helpers.rs:990-991). Draws stop at a 10-card hand or an empty deck (state/mod.rs:811-830). Tests: engine/tests/s189_hidden_zone_eligibility.rs:150-178 (four hand cards are recycled through the deck and redrawn; Copycat is in the discard) and 181-208 (opponent holds 6, only 4 cards are available, 4 are drawn, so the draw is not a fixed 3). An opponent hand of 4 therefore gives 4 draws.

claim: Copycat shuffled the user's hand into the deck and drew 3 cards on both uses, whether the user's hand held 3 cards (T3) or 1 card (T5), so the draw did not follow the user's own hand size; the opponent's hand size was not recorded.

result.evidence: The engine's draw count is the opponent's hand size (apply_trainer_action.rs:2182, 2194-2196), not the user's own hand size. Drawing 3 whether the user held 3 or 1 is what the engine does if the opponent held 3 both times. The hand goes into the deck (2190-2191).
result.note: The support is only 'inferred' and the opponent's hand size was not recorded, so this fits the engine but doesn't test the count rule. Recording the opponent's card-back count at 230007 ~57s and ~121s would settle it.

claim: Lisia takes two Basic Pokemon with 50 HP or less (50 counts) from the deck into hand, publicly revealed: Eevee (50 HP) and Team Rocket's Rattata (40 HP) in one battle; two Team Rocket's Rattata on turn 2 in another, both then benched.

result.evidence: lisia_effect (engine/src/actions/apply_trainer_action.rs:2299-2308) keeps cards with stage == 0 && hp <= 50, so 50 counts. It takes 2 through card_search_outcomes_with_filter_multiple, one equally likely unordered pair per outcome, then moves them to the hand and shuffles (shared_mutations.rs:137-182). engine/database.json has Eevee B1 184 at HP 50 and Team Rocket's Rattata B4a 058 at HP 40, both stage 0, so both qualify. Duplicate copies count as separate items (combinatorics.rs:16-38), so {Rattata, Rattata} is a possible result. Benching is a separate Place action. The only test is legality: Lisia is blocked with an empty deck (engine/tests/rules_repair_trainers.rs:155-179). No effect test exists.
result.note: 'Publicly revealed' is not established. Both cited Lisias were the recording owner's own (Pocket Deck Lab reviews: 232035 REVIEW.md line 20; 232617 REVIEW.md line 27), so the footage shows only the owner's screen. The engine also shows the owner its own hand and hides the result from the opponent (observation.rs:56), which matches rules/04:149 (Dustin: Lisia included). There is no contradiction on this evidence.

claim: Hiking Trail's hand refill is an end-of-turn Stadium effect: it fired after the turn's attack and any KO, point and promotion, before the Pokemon Checkup, and also once at the end of an opponent's turn (whose hand was not stated).

result.evidence: The Hiking Trail refill is in on_end_turn(player_ending_turn) (engine/src/hooks/core.rs:554-567). on_end_turn runs inside the EndTurn forecast (apply_action_helpers.rs:87-117) before the Checkup phase (forecast_checkup_phase -> apply_pokemon_checkup, lines 109-113, 136, 152). EndTurn is only offered once the move_generation_stack is empty (move_generation/mod.rs:45-66). Attacks set end_turn_pending only after their knockout pass (apply_action_helpers.rs:1078-1088), so attack damage, knockouts, points and promotion choices all resolve first. The order is: attack -> KO/points -> promotion -> on_end_turn (Hiking Trail) -> Pokémon Checkup. Because the refill is keyed to the player whose turn ended, it also fires at the end of the opponent's turn for the opponent. No test covers Hiking Trail.
result.note: Order inside on_end_turn: after the turn player's Bad Dreams/berries, delayed damage, Metal Core Barrier and Zeraora; before Soothing Shore, Deceptive Needle and the other player's berries/Bad Dreams (core.rs:413-575). This matches rules/03 §5 (end-of-turn effects before the Checkup).

claim: Hiking Trail refills the hand to 3 cards: from 1 card it added 2 (Cyrus and Rare Candy beside a held Flame Patch), and from 2 cards it added 1 (Mega Blaziken ex).

result.evidence: engine/src/hooks/core.rs:555-566: if the hand has fewer than 3 cards, draw 3 - hand_size times with maybe_draw_card (appends to the hand; stops at an empty deck or a 10-card hand, state/mod.rs:811-830). A hand of 1 draws 2 (Cyrus and Rare Candy beside Flame Patch, 232955 T7) and a hand of 2 draws 1 (Mega Blaziken ex, 230007 T3). No test covers Hiking Trail.

claim: Sightseer publicly revealed the card it took into hand, a Stage 1 Team Rocket's Raticate ex.

result.evidence: What the engine takes matches the claim. sightseer_effect uses top_n_reveal_outcomes(…, 4, stage == 1) (apply_trainer_action.rs:2380-2389; shared_mutations.rs:433-482). It puts every Stage 1 card among the top min(4, deck) into the hand, so Team Rocket's Raticate ex (Stage 1, B4a 059) qualifies. The engine does not reveal the result to the opponent: there is no reveal event, and the opponent sees card backs (observation.rs:56, 678-683; public_reveal_events is only pushed at apply_attack_action.rs:5474-5481).
result.note: The cited Sightseer (022627 T7) was the recording owner's own (Pocket Deck Lab 022627 REVIEW.md line 26: Dacz8976 plays it; that review says 'views the top three cards', which fits a short deck). The footage therefore shows only the owner's screen and cannot show whether the opponent saw the card. Dustin's general rule (rules/04:149, any deck-to-hand card is hidden) points toward the engine. An opponent-seat view of a Sightseer, or Dustin's confirmation, would settle it.

claim: Clemont took two Clemont's Backpacks from the deck into hand, shown to the owner, and both Items were played that same turn.

result.evidence: clemont_effect (apply_trainer_action.rs:2366-2372) takes 2 random cards among Magneton, Heliolisk and Clemont's Backpack through card_search_outcomes_with_filter_multiple (shared_mutations.rs:137-182). generate_combinations treats duplicate copies as separate items (combinatorics.rs:16-38), so two Backpacks is a possible result. They go to the hand and the deck is shuffled. Backpack is always playable (move_generation_trainer.rs:261) with no per-turn Item limit. Each play adds its own +20 TurnEffect (apply_trainer_action.rs:2355-2364), and turn effects are summed in hooks/core.rs:1038-1081, so both apply. The owner sees its own hand (observation masks only the opponent's, observation.rs:56). Tests: Clemont legality only (engine/tests/rules_repair_trainers.rs:111-142). This is the same battle as rules/04:75 (trial-manectric: two Backpacks both added +20).

claim: Professor's Research goes to the discard and draws exactly 2 cards, which are added to the existing hand; the hand is not replaced (it drew two Revavroom).

result.evidence: When played, a non-Tool, non-Stadium Trainer is first moved from hand to discard (apply_common_action_prefix, engine/src/actions/apply_action_helpers.rs:975-992). Then professor_oak_effect draws exactly 2 through maybe_draw_card (apply_trainer_action.rs:1850-1855). That pushes onto the existing hand and does not replace it (state/mod.rs:819-820), within the 10-card and empty-deck limits. Tests cover only legality: an empty deck blocks it, one card allows it (engine/tests/s187_f017_professors_research.rs:61-89). No test checks the draw effect.

claim: Pokemon Communication swaps 1-for-1: a chosen hand Pokemon goes into the deck and a deck Pokemon joins the hand (hand 5 after use 1, 4 after use 2); the Mega Sharpedo EX put in by use 1 came back out on use 2.

result.evidence: Legal with a Pokémon in hand and a nonempty deck (move_generation_trainer.rs:689-702). The card is discarded on play (apply_action_helpers.rs:990-991). pokemon_communication_effect lets the player choose which hand Pokémon to swap (apply_trainer_action.rs:1931-1944). forecast_pokemon_communication (engine/src/actions/apply_action.rs:1544-1588) picks the deck Pokémon uniformly from the deck as it was before the swap (1566-1570). It then moves the chosen hand Pokémon into the deck (1574), moves the picked Pokémon to the hand (1576) and shuffles (1578). Each use is 1-for-1, so the hand goes down by 1 per use (the Communication card itself), e.g. 5 then 4. A card put into the deck by use 1, such as Mega Sharpedo ex (a Stage 1 Pokémon, B4 035), can be drawn by use 2. Test: legality only (engine/tests/rules_repair_trainers.rs:144-152).
result.note: The claim's 'Mega Sharpedo EX' is the card database's 'Mega Sharpedo ex'. Order within one use: the random pick excludes the Pokémon being put in on that same use.

claim: A Pokemon can attack the turn it evolves: Lucario (Submarine Blow, T5), Rampardos (Head Smash, T13), Team Rocket's Electrode (Random Spark, T8, after a free retreat to Active), Naclstack (Rock Throw 50, KOing Magmar, T4), Ivysaur (Synthesis, via Quick-Grow Extract), Slowking ex (Hand Kinesis), Mega Altaria ex (T4).

result.evidence: Evolving never ends the turn or blocks attacking. apply_evolve (engine/src/actions/apply_action.rs:1503-1542) swaps in the new card and does not set end_turn_pending. generate_attack_actions (engine/src/move_generation/attacks.rs:14-80) has no played_this_turn or 'evolved this turn' gate. The strongest evidence is a legality-checked test, engine/tests/rules_repair_attacker_debuff.rs:62-78: `choose` only picks actions from generate_possible_actions. In it, Rattata evolves into Raticate on T4 (line 73) and Raticate's attack is then offered and resolves in the same turn (lines 75-77). Evolving from deck works the same way: Quick-Grow Extract resolves through apply_evolve (apply_trainer_action.rs:2412-2433 and 2462ff; test sunflora_quick_grow_beam_test.rs:12-73), so Ivysaur can use Synthesis. The printed lines match the database: Lucario and Riolu, Naclstack and Nacli (database.rs:69955-69958), Team Rocket's Electrode and Voltorb (79560-79563), Team Rocket's Slowking ex and Slowpoke (79700-79703), Mega Altaria ex and Swablu (46108-46111), Rampardos and Cranidos (10706-10711).
result.note: Also consistent: engine/tests/pokemon/energy_discard_combo_attacks_test.rs:271-306 evolves Dudunsparce and then attacks in the same turn, but it applies actions directly, without a legality check. Whether Electrode's retreat was free is a retreat-cost question, not an evolution one.

claim: Skull Fossil can be played onto the Bench as a 40-HP Basic Pokemon (T7), then evolved into Cranidos at 90 HP (T9) and later into Rampardos at 150 HP (T13).

result.evidence: Fossils are played through the trainer path. engine/src/move_generation/move_generation_trainer.rs:94-97 routes TrainerType::Fossil to can_place_fossil (937-953), which offers Place into any empty slot, the Bench included. Skull Fossil is TrainerType::Fossil (database.rs:12004-12011). Its in-play HP is 40 (hooks/core.rs:90-103; played_card.rs:120-135), and it is placed with played_this_turn=true (apply_action.rs:1097). That flag clears at the next turn change (played_card.rs:460-474). Cranidos is stage 1, evolves_from 'Skull Fossil', HP 90 (database.rs:10684-10691). Rampardos is stage 2, evolves_from 'Cranidos', HP 150 (10706-10711). can_evolve_into compares evolves_from with the fossil's trainer name (models/card.rs:269-272, 160-166). apply_evolve takes the new card's HP (apply_action.rs:1511). Tests: move_generation/mod.rs:340-370 generates a legal Bench evolution of Old Amber into Aerodactyl ex; card_logic/rare_candy.rs:223-231 recognises the Skull Fossil to Cranidos to Rampardos chain.
result.note: No test covers Skull Fossil to Cranidos directly, but the Old Amber test uses the same code path. Side note: the engine does not treat Fossils as Items for Item-lock (move_generation_trainer.rs:65), which does not matter here.

claim: A Pokemon promoted to Active after a KO can evolve on its owner's next turn: Electrike (benched T2) evolved into Mega Manectric ex on T4, and Swablu (benched T5) evolved into Mega Altaria ex on T7.

result.evidence: Promotion does not reset evolution timing. Promote and Activate run apply_retreat(..., is_free=true), which calls apply_activate (engine/src/actions/apply_action.rs:823-830, 1431-1434). Only to_playable_card sets played_this_turn (grep: apply_action.rs:1097, 1337, 1511), and it is cleared for every in-play Pokemon at each advance_turn (state/mod.rs:1186-1208, calling played_card.rs:460-474). A Pokemon benched on T2 or T5 and promoted during the opponent's turn therefore passes the hand-evolution gate on its owner's next turn: turn_count>2 and !played_this_turn (move_generation/mod.rs:209-212). Mega Manectric ex evolves from Electrike (database.rs:62085-62088) and Mega Altaria ex from Swablu (46108-46111). The legality-checked test rules_repair_attacker_debuff.rs:62-78 shows a benched-before Pokemon evolving on a later owner turn.

claim: Mega Gyarados ex evolves directly from Magikarp as a normal evolution from hand (Wallace not used).

result.evidence: Mega Gyarados ex is stored as stage 1 with evolves_from 'Magikarp' in every printing (engine/src/database.rs:44942-44945, 49440-49443, 50039-50042, 73800-73803). So Card::can_evolve_into (models/card.rs:269-272) and the normal hand-evolution generator (move_generation/mod.rs:195-219) offer it as an ordinary Evolve from hand, with from_deck:false. No Wallace or Waterfall Evolution is needed.

claim: Rare Candy worked on its user's 2nd turn (T3 going first, T4 going second) on Basics benched the previous turn or in play since setup: Dratini to Dragonite (T3, T7), Deino to Hydreigon (T4); also twice in one turn on two Torchic, and the turn it was drawn.

result.evidence: can_play_rare_candy (engine/src/move_generation/move_generation_trainer.rs:663-685) blocks Rare Candy only when is_users_first_turn(), meaning turn_count<=2 (state/mod.rs:1227-1229), or when Evolution Jammer is active. T3 (going first) and T4 (going second) are therefore allowed. can_rare_candy_evolve (card_logic/rare_candy.rs:94-110) needs a stage 0 target that is not played_this_turn. A Basic benched on the previous own turn, or in play since setup, qualifies once end_turn_maintenance has cleared the flag (played_card.rs:472). The Stage 1 to Stage 2 lookup table (rare_candy.rs:57-90) covers Dratini to Dragonite, Deino to Hydreigon, and Torchic to Mega Blaziken ex (stage 2 from Combusken, database.rs:44561-44564). Nothing checks when the Rare Candy was drawn. Items are unlimited and each play re-checks pairs (apply_trainer_action.rs:1904-1928). The first Torchic becomes a played-this-turn Stage 2 and drops out, so the second Torchic is still a valid target.
result.note: Only unit tests exist for the lookup (rare_candy.rs:193-231); no game-level Rare Candy test. Already known and not part of this claim: Rare Candy ignores Primeval Law.

claim: A Pokemon can retreat using Energy attached that same turn and then be evolved on the Bench later that turn: Active Gible paid its retreat with the just-attached Fighting and became Gabite on the Bench.

result.evidence: Retreat is offered whenever the Active's current attached Energy covers the cost, with no check on when it was attached (engine/src/move_generation/mod.rs:94-105). finish_paid_retreat discards the chosen Energy, sets has_retreated and swaps the Pokemon (apply_action.rs:1431-1468). Retreat never touches played_this_turn. Gible in play since setup, on T3, therefore still passes the hand-evolution gate on the Bench (mod.rs:209-212). Primeval Law restricts only slot 0 (mod.rs:252-258), and no retreat-related flag blocks evolution. Gabite evolves_from 'Gible' (database.rs:11489-11492 and others).
result.note: No dedicated test for retreat followed by Bench evolution in the same turn; the verdict rests on code paths.

claim: A Pokemon in play since setup can evolve on its owner's second turn: Gible to Gabite and Electrike to Mega Manectric ex on T3 (going first), Koffing to Weezing ex on T3, and Nacli to Naclstack on T4 (going second).

result.evidence: is_users_first_turn() is turn_count<=2 (engine/src/state/mod.rs:1227-1229), so evolution is blocked on T1 and T2 and allowed from T3 (first player) and T4 (second player) (move_generation/mod.rs:209-212). Setup placements are cleared when the game starts (apply_action_helpers.rs:73-74, which calls end_turn_maintenance). Tests: engine/tests/engine/apply_actions_test.rs:37-68 checks that no evolution happens on turns 1-2. boiler_smog_public_forecast_test.rs:25-61 finds Team Rocket's Koffing to Team Rocket's Weezing ex among the legal actions at turn_count 3. rules_repair_attacker_debuff.rs:62-78 legally evolves the second player's Rattata on T4. Naclstack evolves from Nacli (database.rs:69955-69958) and Mega Manectric ex from Electrike (62085-62088).
result.note: The Koffing-to-Weezing ex T3 citation is 'inferred' in the claim's support, but the engine matches either way.

claim: Evolution went one stage per owner turn, and a Pokemon evolved on one turn could evolve again on its owner's next turn: Gabite (T3) to Garchomp (T5); Machop (Benched T14) to Machoke (T16) to Machamp ex (T18); Grimer (T15) to Muk (T17).

result.evidence: apply_evolve builds the evolved card with played_this_turn=true (engine/src/actions/apply_action.rs:1511). The hand-evolution gate requires !played_this_turn (move_generation/mod.rs:210), so the same Pokemon cannot evolve twice in one turn. Rare Candy also requires a stage 0 target that was not played this turn (card_logic/rare_candy.rs:97-100). The flag clears at every advance_turn (state/mod.rs:1205, calling played_card.rs:472), so the Pokemon can evolve again on its owner's next turn. The same applies to a Pokemon benched that turn (apply_action.rs:1097). This gives Gabite T3 then Garchomp T5; Machop benched T14, Machoke T16, Machamp ex T18; Grimer T15, Muk T17.
result.note: The engine does allow skipping a stage with Rare Candy; the claim covers only normal evolution.

claim: Eevee ex can evolve into a non-ex Sylveon (90 max HP), not only into Sylveon ex.

result.evidence: hooks::can_evolve_into (engine/src/hooks/core.rs:125-137) allows any card whose evolves_from is 'Eevee' when the base has CanEvolveIntoEeveeEvolution. Veevee 'volve text maps to that mechanic (actions/effect_ability_mechanic_map.rs:567-570). Non-ex Sylveon A3b 033 is stage 1, evolves_from 'Eevee', HP 90 (database.rs:26344-26347). Normal timing still applies because only Boosted Evolution bypasses it (move_generation/mod.rs:199-212). Tests: tests/pokemon/legacy_ability_logic_test.rs:719-738 legally evolves Eevee ex into the non-ex Vaporeon; hooks/core.rs:2742-2764 covers Eevee ex to Vaporeon and rejects Charizard.

claim: Aerodactyl ex's Primeval Law reads that the opponent can't play Pokemon from hand to evolve their Active Pokemon; its notice appeared as soon as Old Amber evolved into Aerodactyl ex on the Bench, before X Speed made it Active.

result.evidence: Primeval Law text maps to PreventOpponentActiveEvolution (engine/src/actions/effect_ability_mechanic_map.rs:682-685). can_evolve_at_position blocks hand evolution only at position 0, the opponent's Active (move_generation/mod.rs:252-258). has_opponent_aerodactyl_ex_primeval_law checks every opponent in-play Pokemon, Bench included (mod.rs:270-282). The engine therefore treats the Ability as live as soon as Aerodactyl ex is on the Bench, which fits the notice appearing before X Speed moved it up. Old Amber evolves into Aerodactyl ex on the Bench (database.rs:7771-7774; test mod.rs:340-370). Blocking tests: mod.rs:372-408 and tests/pokemon/legacy_ability_logic_test.rs:160-177, both with Aerodactyl ex Active.
result.note: No test puts Aerodactyl ex on the Bench; the Bench-live behaviour rests on the code at mod.rs:274-281. The engine has no notice UI; this verdict covers the rule effect only. Already known and outside this claim: Rare Candy ignores Primeval Law.

claim: Primeval Law does not stop Bench evolution: with the opponent's Aerodactyl ex Active, the owner evolved Benched Vibrava into Flygon ex (180 HP) while the Active Dartrix stayed unevolved.

result.evidence: Primeval Law blocks only in_play_idx 0 (engine/src/move_generation/mod.rs:252-258), so Bench hand evolution stays legal. The test mod.rs:410-450 (test_aerodactyl_ex_does_not_block_bench_evolution) asserts that a Bench Evolve is generated while the opponent has Aerodactyl ex, and mod.rs:372-408 asserts the Active cannot evolve. Flygon ex is stage 2, evolves_from 'Vibrava', HP 180 (database.rs:66894-66897).

claim: Eevee, Active since setup, evolved into Jolteon ex via Boosted Evolution on its owner's first turn (T2), then received Lightning and did not attack, so Boosted Evolution is not an attack and allows evolving on that first turn.

result.evidence: Boosted Evolution text maps to the passive mechanic CanEvolveOnFirstTurnIfActive (engine/src/actions/effect_ability_mechanic_map.rs:36-39). It is not activatable: move_generation_abilities.rs:228 returns false and apply_abilities_action.rs:324-325 calls it passive. It is not an attack. When the Eevee carrying it is Active (i==0), hand evolution skips both the first-turn gate (turn_count<=2 covers T2, state/mod.rs:1227-1229) and the played-this-turn gate (move_generation/mod.rs:198-212). Jolteon ex evolves_from 'Eevee' (database.rs:45629-45632). Attaching Energy and ending the turn without attacking remain available (mod.rs:69-92). Tests: tests/pokemon/additional_ability_logic_test.rs:149-166 (turn_count 1, Active B1 184 Eevee, Evolve generated) and tests/rules_repair_status_evolution.rs:60-84 (exception applies only to the Active Eevee).
result.note: The tests use turn_count 1 rather than T2, but the same is_users_first_turn branch covers T2. The claim is marked as contradicting first-pass R67; the engine agrees with this second-pass reading.

claim: Attached Energy stays on a Pokemon through evolution, including Mega evolution (Swablu's 1 Psychic stayed on Mega Altaria ex) and Rare Candy evolution (Goomy's 2 Psychic stayed on Hisuian Goodra, which then had Water + 2 Psychic).

result.evidence: Every evolution path, including Mega evolution and Rare Candy, goes through the same function, apply_evolve (engine/src/actions/apply_action.rs:1503-1542). At line 1523 it copies the energy across: `played_card.attached_energy = from_pokemon.attached_energy.clone();`. Damage (1521-1522), Tools (1524) and cards_behind (1525-1526) are carried the same way. How each case reaches it: (1) Normal and Mega evolution from hand. move_generation/mod.rs:214-218 emits SimpleAction::Evolve, and apply_action.rs:818-822 sends that to apply_evolve. The engine has no separate Mega-evolution code path. Mega Altaria ex is an ordinary Stage 1 from Swablu (lib/card.py 'Mega Altaria ex' gives 'Stage 1 (from Swablu)', and database.rs has evolves_from "Swablu"). (2) Rare Candy. rare_candy_effect (apply_trainer_action.rs:1905-1928) pushes SimpleAction::Evolve { from_deck: false } (line 1915), so it lands in the same apply_evolve. The Goomy to Hisuian Goodra pair is legal in RARE_CANDY_LOOKUP (card_logic/rare_candy.rs:57-90), because Hisuian Sliggoo has evolves_from "Goomy" (database.rs:72716) and Hisuian Goodra has evolves_from "Hisuian Sliggoo" (database.rs:72740). After apply_evolve, on_evolve (hooks/core.rs:140-268) only runs on-evolve Abilities. Neither Mega Altaria ex nor Hisuian Goodra has one, and no branch in it touches the evolving Pokemon's own Energy. Test: the unit test test_apply_evolve (apply_action.rs:1848-1901) evolves a Mankey into Primeape twice, once Active with 1 Energy and 30 damage, once Benched with 3 Energy. It asserts attached_energy is unchanged, [energy] at 1871 and [energy,energy,energy] at 1896. This matches the in-game text recorded in rules/04_actions_cards_effects.md:43, which says an evolved Pokemon keeps all attached Energy and any damage. rules/README.md lists no open bug about Energy on evolution. Engine source is the same at 7fc6ccb and HEAD (git diff 7fc6ccb HEAD -- engine/src is empty, and the working tree has no local changes).
result.note: Order: the energy copy happens inside apply_evolve before the evolution card leaves the hand (1533-1538) and before the on_evolve hooks run (1541). So the evolved Pokemon already has its Energy when any on-evolve Ability resolves. No test drives a Mega or Rare Candy evolution through the public Game API and checks Energy. Coverage for those two cases rests on the shared code path plus the Mankey to Primeape unit test. I tried to re-run test_apply_evolve myself (cargo test --release --features test-utils --lib test_apply_evolve). It timed out at 580s while compiling, because other agents' cargo builds were running at the same time. So I am citing the test source, not a fresh pass. A game-level test that evolves Swablu into Mega Altaria ex, and Goomy into Hisuian Goodra with Rare Candy, then asserts attached_energy, would close that gap. Relation to R186/R183: this refines them. Both the Mega and Rare Candy cases resolve through apply_evolve line 1523.

claim: Training Area's +10 hits only the opposing Active; each Clemont's Backpack adds 20 to every target. Heliolisk's Electrispark (40 Active, 10 per Benched) did 50 and 10 each with Training Area alone (Bench 110->100, 70->60, 60->50), and 90 and 50 each with two Backpacks added.

result.evidence: engine/src/hooks/core.rs:1737 defines is_active_to_active (target slot 0, attacker slot 0, from an attack). core.rs:1817-1832 adds Training Area only when that is true, via stadiums.rs:131-137 (stage == 1). Clemont's Backpack (apply_trainer_action.rs:2355-2364) adds a TurnEffect of +20 for Magneton/Heliolisk. core.rs:1069-1087 exempts it from the Active-only gate (the is_backpack check), and the .sum() at core.rs:1113 stacks two copies. Test engine/tests/rules_repair_damage_opening.rs:135-170: B4 061 Heliolisk Electrispark with Backpack does 30 to a Benched Pokemon, and with Giovanni does 10. Heliolisk B4 061 is Stage 1 per card.py. Engine numbers: Training Area alone gives 40+10=50 to the Active and 10 to each Benched. With two Backpacks: 40+10+20+20=90 to the Active and 10+20+20=50 to each Benched.
result.note: Training Area plus two Backpacks together has no test; the result follows from the code. rules/02 line 68 still says the Backpack is Active-only. That is stale: audit item M2 has been repaired (rules/09 line 15).

claim: When Ilima returned the damaged Active Raticate ex to hand, its owner promoted a Benched Pokemon (Alolan Vulpix) immediately, before any other action, and could still bench a Basic Rattata from hand later that turn.

result.evidence: Ilima (apply_trainer_action.rs:1836-1846) queues ReturnPokemonToHand. apply_action.rs:1173-1188 moves the Pokemon to hand and, when slot 0 was taken, calls trigger_promotion_or_declare_winner (state/mod.rs:1361-1399). That queues a stack frame holding only Promote choices, so the promotion is the owner's next decision before any other action. Tests: src/players/promotion_continuation_tests.rs:657-679 (the stack is exactly one frame, [promote bench 1]) and tests/trainers/ilima_test.rs:61-108. After the stack clears, the turn continues with ordinary hand actions, so a Basic can be benched later.
result.note: No test benches a Basic after the Ilima promotion; that part follows from normal move generation. The engine also discards the returned Pokemon's Energy and Tools (apply_action.rs:1180-1181), which the claim does not mention.

claim: Rainbow Cave's Energy conversion is used by both players, happens before and apart from the turn's normal Energy attachment, and does not count as that attachment (8 and 7 normal attachments tallied separately).

result.evidence: stadiums.rs:199-205 can_use_rainbow_cave takes a per-player has_used_stadium flag and requires a generated Energy (energy_zone.current is Some). move_generation/mod.rs:119-127 offers UseStadium to whoever is current_player, and state/mod.rs:955 resets the flag each turn, so both players can use it. apply_stadium_action.rs:80-93 discards the current Energy and rotates the zone without touching the attachment. Test tests/stadiums/rainbow_cave_test.rs:93-111: after Rainbow Cave, the new Energy is still offered as an Attach with is_turn_energy: true, so the normal attachment is not used up.
result.note: The engine offers Rainbow Cave only before the turn's attachment: after attaching, current is None (rainbow_cave_test.rs:80-90). That agrees with the claim that it came before the normal attachment. Tests only exercise player 0; player 1 follows from the per-player code.

claim: Training Area's +10 applies only to Stage 1 attackers: Basic Tapu Koko ex's Mach Bolt got none (90 to 100 came from Giovanni alone), while Mega Manectric ex and Mega Altaria ex (evolved from Basics) got +10. Whether it boosts the opponent's Stage 1 (Ivysaur) was untested.

result.evidence: stadiums.rs:131-137 gives +10 only when attacker_stage == 1. core.rs:1820 reads the stage from the card (core.rs:105-107). card.py: Tapu Koko ex is Stage 0, Mega Manectric ex is Stage 1 (from Electrike), Mega Altaria ex is Stage 1 (from Swablu). So Mach Bolt gets 90 + Giovanni's 10 (apply_trainer_action.rs:914-917) = 100, and both Megas get +10. Tests: tests/stadiums/stadium_test.rs:381-423 (no bonus for a Basic), :425-472 (none for Stage 2), :323-379 (Stage 1 Ivysaur gets +10). The code has no owner check, so the opponent's Stage 1 is boosted too (stadium_test.rs:682-722 sets up Training Area as a shared Stadium).
result.note: The claim's support is only inferred, but the engine agrees with it. The Stage 1 test in stadium_test.rs:682-722 has only player 0 attack; the two-sided effect follows from the code.

claim: Sitrus Berry can also trigger at the end of its holder's own turn. Attached on owner T7 to Revavroom at 10/120 HP, it healed once (10->40) late in that same turn.

result.evidence: hooks/core.rs:413-416 runs apply_end_of_turn_berries_for_owner for the player whose turn is ending. core.rs:573-574 then runs it for the other player, so Sitrus Berry checks at the end of both players' turns. core.rs:2261-2286 heals 30 when remaining HP x2 <= max, then discards the Berry. Test tests/tools/berries_test.rs:91-122: player 0's own EndTurn heals player 0's Sitrus holder (60 to 90) and discards the Berry. Revavroom B4 115 has 120 HP (card.py), so 10/120 heals once to 40.
result.note: Timing within the end-of-turn sequence: the ending player's Bad Dreams resolves first, then their Berries.

claim: Kid's Room shuffles the hand card given up into the deck, not the discard, then gives a random Pokemon Tool that can be attached the same turn: a traded Flame Patch was drawn again T9 and T11; a traded Professor's Research brought Sitrus Berry, attached to Benched Varoom.

result.evidence: apply_stadium_action.rs:152-170 queues one SwitchHandCardForRandomTool choice per hand card. apply_stadium_action.rs:177-213 moves the chosen card from hand to deck (state/mod.rs:904-912 transfer_card_from_hand_to_deck), draws a uniformly random Tool from the deck to hand, and shuffles. Nothing goes to the discard pile. Test tests/stadiums/kids_room_test.rs:89-151: Potion ends up in the deck and Rocky Helmet in the hand. The drawn Tool is an ordinary hand card, so it can be attached the same turn under normal Tool play (tools.rs:119-133).
result.note: No test attaches the Tool in the same turn; that follows from normal move generation. If the deck has no Tool, the engine only shuffles and the chosen card stays in hand (apply_stadium_action.rs:190-195).

claim: Both players used Mesagoza on their own turns (owner T4 and T6, opponent T5 and T7). The owner's T6 Heads put a Stage 1 Glimmora into hand, so its random Pokemon search is not limited to Basics.

result.evidence: Mesagoza's search (apply_stadium_action.rs:118-139) calls pokemon_search_outcomes(acting_player, state, false). With basic_only=false, shared_mutations.rs:16-28 matches any Card::Pokemon, so a Stage 1 Glimmora can be found. Test tests/stadiums/stadium_test.rs:800-851: after player 0 uses Mesagoza and ends the turn, player 1 is offered UseStadium. Each player's once-per-turn flag resets at state/mod.rs:955.
result.note: No test puts a Stage 1 into hand with Mesagoza; the code sets no Basic filter.

claim: A played Stadium stays in play until replaced or removed, and its effect can be used on later turns: Rainbow Cave was used T2, T4, T12 and T16; Peculiar Plaza stayed T4-T7; Area Zero, played T9, was activated T13 (literal banner), resolving a hidden face-down card exchange.

result.evidence: The Stadium sits in state.active_stadium and leaves only when replaced (tests/stadiums/stadium_test.rs:261-317) or removed (the DiscardActiveStadium action, apply_action.rs:914-918). Activated effects are gated only by a per-turn flag that resets at the end of each turn (state/mod.rs:955), so they can be used on any later turn: stadium_test.rs:800-851 uses Mesagoza on a later turn. Area Zero: stadiums.rs:180-189 (usable while a Basic is in hand) and apply_stadium_action.rs:95-114 (shuffle a Basic into the deck, draw 1). Test tests/stadiums/area_zero_test.rs:83-131. Peculiar Plaza is passive (retreat.rs:207-213) and applies while it is the active Stadium.

claim: Future Booster Energy Capsule attached to the Active Iron Bundle ex showed a +20 banner as its effect. Iron Bundle ex never attacked, so the bonus was never applied.

result.evidence: hooks/core.rs:49-61 lists Iron Bundle ex as a Future Pokemon. core.rs:1515-1523 gives +20 per Capsule. core.rs:1805-1809 applies it only inside attack damage and only Active-to-Active. Attaching the Capsule changes nothing else, so with no attack the bonus never applies. Test tests/tools/booster_capsule_test.rs:79-112 (Future Iron Moth: 50+20 knocks out a 70-HP Bulbasaur) and :114-151 (no bonus for a non-Future Pokemon).
result.note: The engine has no banners; the recording never exercised the +20, so this is consistent but untested by the video.

claim: Erika healed 50 damage from one of its player's Pokemon.

result.evidence: apply_trainer_action.rs:505-507 erika_effect calls inner_healing_effect with 50 and Grass. apply_trainer_action.rs:784-808 offers one Heal { amount: 50 } choice per damaged Grass Pokemon of the acting player. move_generation_trainer.rs:461+ makes Erika playable only when a damaged Grass Pokemon exists.
result.note: The card text (card.py) limits Erika to 1 of your [G] Pokemon, and the engine enforces that; the claim leaves the Grass condition out. No Erika-specific heal test was found.

claim: A Stadium or Tool held in hand has no effect. Starting Plains and Steel Apron stayed in hand all game, and neither affected any observed damage or HP (including Turbo Shark's 0 and Hailstorm's 60).

result.evidence: Stadium effects read only state.active_stadium: stadiums.rs:106-113 has_stadium and :115-117 is_starting_plains_active. claim: Team Rocket Grunt flips coins until the first Tails and removes 1 opposing Energy per Heads, not one flip per attached Energy: Heads-Heads-Tails removed both Fighting from Haxorus; another use went Heads x3 then Tails; a first-flip Tails removed nothing.
related_first_pass: R94 (coin per Energy); agrees with R168

result.evidence: engine/src/actions/apply_trainer_action.rs:2511-2540 (team_rocket_grunt_outcomes): the engine flips until the first Tails, and for each Heads it discards one random Energy from the opposing Active using rng.gen_range. When the Active has no Energy left, the loop breaks. The coin classes come from engine/src/actions/outcomes.rs:138-171 (saturated_geometric_classes): classes 0..K-1 are exact H^k T sequences, and the last class means 'at least K heads' (K = attached Energy count). So H-H-T on 2 Fighting removes both, H-H-H-T removes up to 3, and a first-flip T removes nothing. There is no per-Energy flip anywhere in this code. Legality needs Energy on the opposing Active (move_generation_trainer.rs:1008-1023).
result.note: No dedicated test for Team Rocket Grunt was found under engine/tests, so this rests on reading the code. The Energy is chosen at random, not taken from the end, so the already-known 'take the last Energy' deviation doesn't apply here.

claim: Metal Core Barrier is discarded at the end of the opponent's turn following attachment, not right after the hit: attached T6, it cut Wild Swing on T7 and was discarded at T7's end; on Aegislash it stayed through the opponent's next turn, gone by owner T11.
related_first_pass: R130 (discarded immediately after the hit); agrees with R95

result.evidence: engine/src/hooks/core.rs:504-519 (in on_end_turn): tool_owner = (player_ending_turn+1)%2, and Metal Core Barrier is discarded only from that player's Pokémon. So when the owner ends the turn it was attached (T6), the card is kept. It then gives -50 to a Metal holder against attacks during the opponent's turn (core.rs:728-732) and is discarded at the end of that opponent turn (T7). Nothing discards it on being hit. Test: engine/tests/revavroom_tools_test.rs:664-681 (two_metal_core_barriers_both_expire_at_end_of_opponents_turn), where player 1 ends the turn and player 0's Barriers go to the discard pile.
result.note: No test directly checks that it survives the owner's own end of turn, but the code only strips the player who is not ending the turn.

claim: Starting Plains' +20 raises both max and current HP of every Basic, keeping existing damage (Arceus ex 120/140 to 140/160, then a 20-damage Slash took it to 120; Castform 10 to 30; Mega Diancie ex 120 to 140), but not Stage 1 (Kirlia stayed 80).

Max HP = base + tools + stadium_hp_bonus + ability bonus (played_card.rs:290-310), and remaining = max - damage_counters (276-279). Damage is therefore kept and current HP rises by 20. Bonuses are refreshed after every action (apply_action_helpers.rs:1068 -> state/mod.rs:607-648). Tests: engine/tests/stadiums/stadium_test.rs:478-516 (Basics +20, Stage 1 Ivysaur unchanged) and 518-586 (80 damage kept: 90-HP Bulbasaur shows 10 remaining).

claim: After Team Rocket's Master Plan its user flipped a self-Confusion coin; Heads both times (T5, T7) left its own Active Team Rocket's Magmar unconfused, and it attacked normally.

claim: Hiking Trail's draw (filling a 2-card hand to 3) resolves at end of turn: played before the attack, it drew after Sunny Scorching and before the Burn Checkup. In another game (played T6) it triggered at the end of its owner's T10; that effect was not recorded.

result.evidence: engine/src/hooks/core.rs:554-567: in on_end_turn, if Hiking Trail is in play, the player whose turn is ending draws (3 - hand size) cards, so a 2-card hand draws 1. on_end_turn runs on EndTurn, which comes after the attack: apply_action_helpers.rs:1082-1088 sets end_turn_pending after an Attack. It also runs before the Checkup: apply_action_helpers.rs:110-115 calls on_end_turn(action.actor) first and then phase(), and apply_pokemon_checkup (286-326) does Poison, then Burn, then Sleep, then Paralysis, then KOs. So the engine order is: Sunny Scorching's Burn (Castform Sunny Form B3 024: Burns 'if a Stadium is in play', database.rs:64535-64541), then the Hiking Trail draw, then the Burn Checkup. It fires at the end of every turn whose ending player is under 3 cards, whichever player played it, which fits a trigger on the owner's T10.
result.note: No engine test covers Hiking Trail (grep of engine/tests finds nothing); this verdict rests on code reading only. Inside on_end_turn, Hiking Trail comes after Bad Dreams, berries, delayed damage, Metal Core Barrier and Zeraora, and before Soothing Shore and Deceptive Needle.

claim: Deceptive Needle on the owner's Active Hoopa ex did 10 to the opposing Active at the end of the owner's turn, after attack damage (Pikachu 30 to 20 after Shadow Bullet on T2; again on T4).

result.evidence: engine/src/hooks/core.rs:571 and 578-603 apply_deceptive_needle_damage. At the end of the holder owner's turn (on_end_turn, after the attack and before the Checkup, per apply_action_helpers.rs:110-115 and 1082-1088), if that player's Active is a Darkness Pokémon holding the Needle, it deals 10 per Needle to the opponent's Active. The damage goes through handle_damage with is_from_active_attack=false, so it is not attack damage. Hoopa ex is [D] (card.py B4 103), so Pikachu 30 -> 20 after Shadow Bullet is exactly what the engine does. Test: engine/tests/tools/deceptive_needle_test.rs:17-42 (10 to the opposing Active at the end of the holder's turn).

claim: Misty's result is shown as a Heads/Tails counter; it read 0 Heads, 1 Tails and attached no Energy, a format that fits flipping until Tails.

claim: Cyrus only swaps positions: it pulled the owner's damaged Benched Mega Manectric ex (80 HP) into the Active Spot with its Lightning still attached, and Heliolisk, sent to the Bench, kept its own Energy.

result.evidence: apply_trainer_action.rs:871-885 cyrus_effect offers Activate only for the opponent's damaged Benched Pokémon. Activate goes through apply_action.rs:823-830, then apply_retreat(is_free=true), then apply_action_helpers.rs:939-966 apply_activate. That does in_play_pokemon.swap(0, bench_idx), moving whole PlayedCards, so attached Energy and damage go with each Pokémon. The Pokémon sent to the Bench only has its status and effects cleared, and no Energy is paid or discarded. Test: engine/src/actions/apply_action.rs:1903-1931 test_forcefully_retreat (Activate swaps the two PlayedCards unchanged).

claim: Rocky Helmet still deals 20 to the attacker when its holder is Knocked Out: Steel Wing (70) KO'd Pachirisu ex, which showed 0 HP during the Helmet step, and the +2 points and Victory came only after.

result.evidence: attack_outcome.rs:134-210 runs in this order: damage (handle_damage_only), then the attack's post-damage effect, then handle_attack_retaliation, then handle_knockouts. apply_action_helpers.rs:593-612 finds the damaged holder still in play at 0 HP and applies get_counterattack_damage (counterattack.rs:13-17, 20 per Rocky Helmet) to the attacker. handle_knockouts_with_prior returns early while a ResolveAttackRetaliation is pending (apply_action_helpers.rs:658-660), and points and the win check come later (711-855). Test: engine/tests/observed_gameplay_outcomes_test.rs:184-207 (holder Lucario KO'd, Helmet still returns 20, points awarded) and :114-161.
result.note: This matches rules/README.md item 4 (Helmet fires even when its holder is KO'd, before points).

claim: Either player can use the Stadium in play: after the owner played Kid's Room on T3, the opponent used Kid's Room's effect on T4, T6 and T8 with no Kid's Room play of its own recorded.

It never checks who played the Stadium. move_generation/mod.rs:118-126 offers UseStadium to the current player. apply_stadium_action.rs:152-170 and 177-212 use the acting player's own hand and deck. claim: Will, played before Xatu's coin-flip attack Life Drain, made that coin heads so Life Drain's effect applied (Mega Lucario ex 180->10).
support: Pokemon TCG Pocket Battles - Luckycad Xatu.mp4 @ 03:30-03:47 (inferred)

support: Pokemon TCG Pocket Battles - Luckycad Xatu.mp4 @ 15:16-15:28 (seen)

In attack_outcome.rs:143-209 the retaliation frame and handle_attack_retaliation run only when resolved damage targets exist, so Poison Barb (counterattack.rs:117-124, applied in apply_action_helpers.rs:602-608) never fires. claim: Potion's heal stops at max HP: Pichu (30 max HP) went 20->30, restoring only 10.

result.evidence: Potion goes through inner_healing_effect(20) (apply_trainer_action.rs:667-669 and 784-808; only damaged targets are offered), then SimpleAction::Heal, then apply_healing (apply_action.rs:1246-1262), then State::heal_pokemon (state/mod.rs:863-873), then PlayedCard::heal_raw. heal_raw does damage_counters.saturating_sub(amount) (state/played_card.rs:227-229), so a 30-HP Pichu with 10 damage is healed only 10, back to 30. Shared-primitive cap test: engine/tests/pokemon/delibird_box_of_surprises_test.rs:78-104 (heal_pokemon heal capped at full HP).

claim: More than one Item can be played in a turn: two Poke Balls on T2 both resolved with no failure notice, and Helioptile and Electrike entered play.

result.evidence: The engine has no per-turn Item limit. generate_possible_trainer_actions (engine/src/move_generation/move_generation_trainer.rs:65-67) blocks an Item only when can_play_item returns false. can_play_item (engine/src/hooks/core.rs:678-685) returns false only when a TurnEffect::NoItemCards lock is active; nothing counts Items played. When an Item is played, apply_common_action_prefix (engine/src/actions/apply_action_helpers.rs:975-995) just discards it from hand (line 991) and sets no flag. Only Supporters set has_played_support (line 994), and a grep of engine/src for played_item, items_played and item_played finds nothing. Poke Ball (both P-A 005 and A2b 111) can be played whenever the deck is not empty (move_generation_trainer.rs:140 and 214, can_play_poke_ball at :564-570). Its effect, pokemon_search_outcomes(acting_player, state, true) at apply_trainer_action.rs:99-101, puts a random Basic from the deck into hand, matching the card text 'Put a random Basic Pokémon from your deck into your hand.' Benching Helioptile and Electrike afterwards are separate, ordinary Place actions. The earlier audit reached the same finding (rules/_research_notes/audit_2026-09-22/core_turn.md:245-246, 'Items unlimited'), and it agrees with RULES_FOR_AGENTS.md:45 and rules/01_game_structure.md:45.
result.note: No engine test plays two Items in one turn; this finding rests on the code path, which has no counter to hit. A test that plays one Poke Ball and then checks that Play{Poke Ball} is still offered would pin it down. Nothing in the open bugs (rules/README.md, rules/09) touches this.

claim: A Tool removed by Field Blower goes to its owner's discard pile: the owner's Field Blower removed the opponent's Heavy Helmet, which then appeared in the opponent's discard.

result.evidence: Field Blower's effect (engine/src/actions/apply_trainer_action.rs:578-602) offers DiscardToolFromPokemon{player, in_play_idx, tool_idx} for every Tool on either player's Pokémon, plus DiscardActiveStadium. That action runs state.discard_tool(*player, ...) (engine/src/actions/apply_action.rs:907-913). discard_tool (engine/src/state/mod.rs:1267-1273) removes the Tool and pushes it to discard_piles[player]. Here player is the owner of the Pokémon holding the Tool, not the player who used Field Blower. There is a test: engine/tests/trainers/field_blower_test.rs:21-86 (test_field_blower_discards_opponents_tool). Player 0 plays Field Blower on player 1's Charmander holding Rocky Helmet, and the test asserts state.discard_piles[1].contains(Rocky Helmet) at lines 82-85. The Field Blower card itself goes to its player's own discard (apply_action_helpers.rs:991). Heavy Helmet (B1 219) is an implemented Tool (hooks/core.rs:687-708), so it follows the same discard path.
result.note: The test uses Rocky Helmet, not Heavy Helmet, but the discard path does not depend on which Tool it is. The earlier trainer audit also rated this as matching (rules/_research_notes/audit_2026-09-22/trainers.md:235, T50).

claim: Rainbow Cave always replaces the current generated Energy with the queued next Energy, even when both are the same type: current Fire with Fire queued gave Fire and the preview advanced to Metal; current Metal with Fire queued gave Fire.

result.evidence: forecast_rainbow_cave_effect (engine/src/actions/apply_stadium_action.rs:80-92) runs unconditionally, in this order. (1) If there is a current Energy, it is pushed to discard_energies[player] (lines 86-89). (2) state.rotate_energy_zone(player, rng) (line 91). rotate_energy_zone (engine/src/state/mod.rs:931-940) sets current = next.take() and then rolls a fresh next from the deck's Energy types. Neither function compares the current and next types, so current Fire with Fire queued gives Fire and a newly rolled preview, and current Metal with Fire queued gives Fire. can_use_rainbow_cave (engine/src/stadiums.rs:201-205) only requires that the stadium is active, that it hasn't been used this turn, and that current.is_some(). claim: The turn's generated Energy waits in the Energy Zone while other cards, Supporters included, resolve, then can be attached: Water to Carvanha after Poke Ball, Research and Giant Cape; Grass to Rowlet after Lusamine; Psychic to Mewtwo ex (1 to 2) after Sabrina; Mega Sharpedo EX after Cabbie.

result.evidence: The turn's Energy is put into energy_zone.current at the start of the turn (engine/src/state/mod.rs:931-932, called from advance_turn at 1205-1207). Normal play clears it in only one place, engine/src/state/energy.rs:26-28, when the turn Energy is attached. At turn end the next rotation overwrites it. A grep of src for writes to energy_zone finds no Trainer effect. The only other readers or writers are Rainbow Cave (apply_stadium_action.rs:86) and an attack that changes the opponent's next Energy type (apply_attack_action.rs:3925). claim: The Energy Zone shows a small preview of the next Energy (e.g. Lightning, Metal); tapping it only previews and attaches nothing. The preview is not an attached Energy and must not be counted; the current generated Energy (Psychic) was still the one attached, to Indeedee ex after Cyrus.

Tests: state/mod.rs:1624-1655 (next is filled at setup; rotation moves next into current). This agrees with rules/01_game_structure.md:70-71.

claim: The turn's generated Energy can go to a Benched Pokemon, including one Benched or evolved earlier that turn: Psychic onto just-Benched Indeedee ex, Slowpoke (T2) and Galarian Corsola (T7), just-evolved Houndstone (T5), and Benched Meloetta (T6).

result.evidence: Switch effects go through apply_activate (engine/src/actions/apply_action_helpers.rs:939-966). It swaps the whole PlayedCard and clears only status and effects (engine/src/state/played_card.rs:378-386), so attached_energy stays with the Pokemon on the Bench. Test: engine/tests/rules_repair_energy_choice.rs:133 and 141 (the Benched Gouging Fire keeps its unpaid Energy after retreating).

claim: Energy discarded to pay a retreat goes to the discard pile and is usable the same turn: Flame Patch reattached the Fire Castform had just discarded onto the newly promoted Mega Blaziken ex (1 to 2 Fire), which then used Mega Burning.

With one legal payment (Castform, retreat cost 1, one Fire) it finishes at once and calls state.discard_energy_from_in_play (apply_action.rs:1464). That function moves the Energy into discard_energies[player] (engine/src/state/mod.rs:1336-1357). A test covers this: engine/tests/mechanics/retreat_test.rs:9-36 (test_retreat_discards_energy_into_discard_energies) checks that both retreat-paid Energy end up in discard_energies. Flame Patch is legal when the Active is Fire-type and discard_energies holds a Fire (engine/src/move_generation/move_generation_trainer.rs:848-865). Retreating sets only has_retreated, and that flag gates only another retreat (hooks/retreat.rs:24), so Items and attacks are still allowed. Flame Patch runs attach_energy_from_discard(actor, 0, [Fire]) (engine/src/actions/apply_trainer_action.rs:2172-2174). That takes the Fire out of the discard pile and puts it on the Active (engine/src/state/energy.rs:55-74), so Mega Blaziken ex goes from 1 to 2 Fire and can pay Mega Burning's [RR] (database.rs:44568-44573). The order retreat, then Flame Patch, then attack is legal within one turn.

claim: Turbo Shark's attachment stacks with the turn's normal Energy attachment on the same Pokemon: manual Water then Turbo Shark took Mega Gyarados ex 2 to 3 to 4 (T11) and Gyarados 2 to 3 to 4 (T7).

Only that attachment clears energy_zone.current (engine/src/state/energy.rs:26-28). Turbo Shark maps to Mechanic::ChargeBench{energies:[Water], target_benched_type:Some(Water)} (engine/src/actions/effect_mechanic_map.rs:3027-3032). energy_bench_attack deals the damage, then offers Attach{is_turn_energy:false} to each Benched Water Pokemon (engine/src/actions/apply_attack_action.rs:2318-2345). So it neither needs nor uses the turn's Zone Energy. apply_attach_energy (apply_action.rs:949-964) and attach_energy_internal (state/energy.rs:87-115) just add to attached_energy with no per-Pokemon or per-turn cap. Manual Water first (2 to 3), then Turbo Shark's Water (3 to 4) on the same Benched Mega Gyarados ex or Gyarados (both Water) is legal and stacks. The closest test is engine/tests/pokemon/kubfu_training_test.rs:20-40: a card-effect Zone attachment leaves energy_zone.current in place.
result.note: No test covers Turbo Shark (B4 035) itself; kubfu_training_test covers the reverse order. The engine resolves Turbo Shark's attachment after its 70 damage, which fits the observed order (manual attachment first, then the attack).

claim: Each player made at most one Energy Zone attachment per turn: going second, 10 Fighting over its 10 turns (T2-T20); going first, 9 Darkness over its 10 turns, fitting no Turn 1 Energy; no acceleration was used.

result.evidence: Setup rolls only a 'next' Energy for each player and leaves current = None, so the player going first has nothing to attach on turn 1 (engine/src/state/mod.rs:768-772). Tests: engine/tests/engine/apply_actions_test.rs:228-249 (test_energy_zone_state_at_start_of_turn_1) and :184-206 (no Attach offered on turn 1). advance_turn calls rotate_energy_zone for the incoming player every turn (state/mod.rs:1186-1208, 931-940). So the player going second gets one Energy on each of T2, T4, ..., T20 (10 turns, test at apply_actions_test.rs:253-280), and the player going first gets one on each of T3, ..., T19 (9 of its 10 turns). A single-type deck always rolls its one type (roll_energy, state/mod.rs:1541-1546). Once the manual attachment is made, current becomes None (state/energy.rs:26-28), and Attach is offered only while current is Some (move_generation/mod.rs:77). That gives at most one Zone attachment per turn without acceleration effects.
result.note: The engine's 30-turn cap (state/mod.rs:1201) does not come into play in a 20-turn game.

claim: A two-type Energy Zone (Metal + Psychic) generates one of its types each turn without strict alternation: Metal on T3, T5, T11 and T13, Psychic on T7, T9 and T15.

result.evidence: Each turn rotate_energy_zone moves next into current and rolls a fresh next with roll_energy (engine/src/state/mod.rs:931-940). roll_energy is `deck.energy_types.choose(rng)`, an independent uniform pick from the deck's declared types each time (state/mod.rs:1541-1546). There is no alternation or memory, so runs like Metal, Metal, Psychic, Psychic, Metal, Metal, Psychic are ordinary outcomes. Test: state/mod.rs:1624-1640 checks that rolled Energy comes from each deck's declared set. The engine's first rolled Energy for the player going first is used on T3, which fits the observed T3 through T15 odd-turn sequence.
result.note: Equal odds is the design stated in rules/01 §4 row 72 (IN-GAME TEXT + COMMUNITY JP guides), but rules/05 line 81 says nobody has published a test of it. One seven-turn sequence shows there is no strict alternation. It says nothing on whether the odds are equal.

claim: Energy of any type can be attached to any Pokemon: Metal went onto the Fire-type Team Rocket's Moltres ex, and Fighting onto Dratini.

result.evidence: Move generation offers the turn attachment Attach{(1, energy, i), is_turn_energy:true} for every occupied slot i. The only check is can_attach_energy_from_zone, a turn effect that blocks Active attachments only. There is no type check between the Energy and the Pokemon (engine/src/move_generation/mod.rs:76-92; state/energy.rs:76-85). apply_attach_energy and attach_energy_internal do not check type either (apply_action.rs:949-964; state/energy.rs:87-115). Test: engine/tests/comfey_recovery_test.rs:416-434 applies a move-generated Fire turn attachment to a Grass Bulbasaur (the helper at :114-119 picks from generated legal actions) and asserts attached_energy == [Fire]. Lines :396-406 do the same with Psychic onto Bulbasaur. So Metal onto the Fire-type Team Rocket's Moltres ex and Fighting onto the Dragon-type Dratini are both legal in the engine.

claim: Confusion does not wear off between turns: Team Rocket's Rattata, Confused by Master Plan on T8, failed its Confusion-flip attacks on T9 and T11 and stayed Active until it was Knocked Out on T12.

result.evidence: Nothing in the Checkup touches Confusion. engine/src/actions/apply_action_helpers.rs:254-284 (collect_checkup_targets) gathers only Asleep, Paralyzed, Poisoned and Burned Pokemon, and apply_pokemon_checkup (286-335) clears only Burned (on Heads), Asleep (on Heads) and Paralyzed. The per-turn upkeep in played_card.rs:460-481 and state/mod.rs:942-958 never clears a status. Confusion is removed only by clear_status_and_effects, cure_status_conditions or clear_status_condition (played_card.rs:378-408, used for going to the Bench, evolving and cure cards), or replaced by Asleep or Paralyzed (set_status_raw, 411-436). Every attack by a Confused Active gets the coin (apply_attack_action.rs:124-127). Test tests/mechanics/confusion_test.rs:10-48 shows Tails does nothing (no damage, no self-damage) and leaves only EndTurn. Master Plan Confuses the opponent's Active (trainer_coin_plan.rs:162-164).
result.note: No test checks that Confusion lasts across several Checkups. pokemon_checkup_test.rs:220-241 only checks that a Confused Active doesn't crash the Checkup. The match rests on the code: no Checkup or turn-change path clears Confusion. The claim's own support is only 'inferred'.

claim: Poison removes 10 HP at the Checkup after every turn, both players' turns: 110->100 (end of owner T8), 100->90 (end of opponent T9), 60->50 (end of owner T10). Re-Poisoning an already Poisoned Pokemon (Venomous Hit) kept the tick at 10.

result.evidence: Every Checkup collects Poisoned Pokemon on both sides, turn player first (apply_action_helpers.rs:262-275), and deals get_poison_damage, which defaults to 10 (218-252, applied at 296-300). Test engine/src/game.rs:474-504 (test_poison): a Poisoned Koffing goes 70->60 after the opponent's turn 1, then 60->50 after its owner's turn 2, so it ticks after both players' turns. tests/rules_repair_timing.rs:84-103 shows both sides' Poisoned Actives ticking in the same Checkup. Test tests/pokemon/modified_poison_damage_test.rs:76-103 confirms ordinary poison ticks 10.

claim: At the Sleep Checkup, Heads wakes the Pokemon. The 'Pokemon Checkup - Asleep' banner appeared, the coin showed Heads, and 'Oricorio recovered from being Asleep' followed. Oricorio then started its next turn awake.

claim: Burn deals its first 20 at the Checkup ending the turn it was inflicted, then 20 at every later Checkup (either player's turn) until Heads cures it. Gardevoir went 130->10 (Mega Burning)->0 (Burn) that same turn, scored before the opponent's turn; Lucario took 20 end T5 (Tails), 20 end T6 (Heads).

result.evidence: apply_action_helpers.rs:262-281 collects Burned Pokemon on both sides at every Checkup. 301-309 deals 20, then that Pokemon's coin, and Heads clears Burned.
