claim: When Burn damage KOs a Pokemon at the Checkup, the Burn coin is still flipped and shown (Tails twice: Gardevoir, Mega Diancie ex; Heads plus recovery message: Kirlia 20->0) before the knockout removal; the point then scores normally (+1, 2-0).
related_first_pass: R226 (KO before the flip); see also R240

result.evidence: The Checkup coin branches are built from the Burned targets collected before any Checkup damage (apply_action_helpers.rs:122-128, collect_checkup_targets 254-284), so a Pokemon that the Burn 20 knocks out still gets its coin. apply_pokemon_checkup deals 20, then applies that coin, Heads clearing Burned (301-309). Tests rules_repair_timing.rs:84-103 and game.rs:516-553 show Checkup Knock Outs scoring (Poison cases).

The coin has no effect on a Pokemon about to be Knocked Out, so the difference is only in what the game shows and in how many chance branches the engine creates. claim: When Sunny Scorching or Mega Burning KO'd the Defending Pokemon (Electrode at 20 and at 70, Zapdos ex at 120), its Burn was still applied to the 0-HP Pokemon, before the Rocky Helmet retaliation banner.

result.evidence: attack_outcome.rs:134-209 (into_mutation) runs in this order: damage (143-155), then the attack's own effect (180-182), then Tool retaliation such as Rocky Helmet (186-201), then Knock Outs (207-209). claim: An end-of-turn Ability resolves after the attack's KO and point award but before the KO'd player promotes: Entei ex's Legendary Pulse drew 1 card after Heliolisk's KO point, then Mega Manectric ex was promoted and T9 began.

result.evidence: Engine order is: KO and point, then promotion, then EndTurn, then Checkup, then T9 starts, then the T9 player's draw, and only then the Legendary Pulse draw. Code: after an attack, apply_action_helpers.rs:1082-1088 sets end_turn_pending. handle_knockouts (apply_action_helpers.rs:874-886) calls trigger_promotion_or_declare_winner, which queues Promote on move_generation_stack (state/mod.rs:1391-1423; comment at 1405-1406 says EndTurn only runs once the stack is empty). move_generation/mod.rs:45-66 serves the stack before EndTurn. Legendary Pulse is only pushed as a DrawCard frame in on_end_turn (hooks/core.rs:381-394). In the normal Checkup path (apply_action_helpers.rs:110-116, 163), advance_turn then pushes the next player's draw on top of it (state/mod.rs:1186-1207, line 1206), so the Pulse draw resolves after T9 begins. Probe: a scratch test outside the repo, built from 7fc6ccb (src diff-identical to the repo). Entei ex [Fire,Fire] Blazing Beatdown on Heliolisk at 10 HP, with Mega Manectric ex on the Bench. Result: pts [1,0] -> Promote{player 1, idx 1} -> EndTurn -> turn=9 cur=1 -> P1 DrawCard -> P0 DrawCard (hand0 0->1). The claim puts the Pulse draw before the promotion and before T9.
result.note: Not in rules/README or 09 as a known bug. The engine follows rules/03 §5 step 1 (KOs, points and promotion before end-of-turn effects). If this one 'seen' observation holds, that doc line needs revising as well as the engine. It could also be display order rather than rules order. Separately, the Pulse draw resolving after the Checkup and after the next player's opening draw breaks rules/03 §5 even on the doc's own order. That part is new.

result.evidence: Dragon's Blessing maps to AttachEnergyFromDiscardToActiveTypedFromBench{Dragon} (effect_ability_mechanic_map.rs:842-848). Resolution offers one AttachTypedFromDiscard per Energy type (apply_abilities_action.rs:387-410). That calls attach_energy_from_discard (apply_action.rs:1724-1737, energy.rs:55-74), which never clears energy_zone.current. So the normal turn attachment (move_generation/mod.rs:77-92, cleared only for is_turn_energy at energy.rs:26-28) is still available, giving 2 Energy that turn.
result.note: No direct gameplay test for Dragon's Blessing: only a value-function test (tests/s117_gtier_test.rs:43-51). This verdict rests on the code.

claim: Electromagnetic Wall stops once Jolteon ex leaves play: after Jolteon ex was knocked out on T5, the opponent's T7 Psychic attachment to Slowking ex (1->2) caused no Wall damage and Slowking stayed at 120.

result.note: No test covers the Wall stopping after Jolteon leaves. The verdict comes from the per-attachment board check.

claim: Evil Inspiration draws exactly 1 card per use; the opponent used it once on each of T4, T5, T6 and T7 across two battles, at varied points in the turn (after Slowking ex became Active, before Elegant Cape, after Sabrina).

result.evidence: Evil Inspiration maps to DrawCardsOncePerTurn{amount:1, require_active:true} (effect_ability_mechanic_map.rs:862-869). It is offered whenever that Pokémon is Active, not used yet, and the deck is non-empty, at any point in the free-action phase (move_generation_abilities.rs:260-264, move_generation/mod.rs:114-116). It resolves as queue_draw_action(actor, 1) (apply_abilities_action.rs:450, 1137-1141). The flag resets each turn (played_card.rs:471-474). Tests: tests/b4a_attack_batch2_test.rs:200-228 (draws exactly 1, then no longer offered) and :230-263 (not offered from the Bench or with an empty deck).

claim: Meloetta's Strange Singing was used only from the Active Spot and did not use up the turn's attack (Slowking ex attacked after it on T4); it put a Pokemon into hand, Basic or Stage 1, and the opponent's results stayed hidden.

result.evidence: Strange Singing maps to StartTurnRandomPokemonToHand{Psychic} (effect_ability_mechanic_map.rs:81-86). It is never an action choice (move_generation_abilities.rs:137). It fires automatically only for the Active of the player starting the turn (apply_action_helpers.rs:190-213, via maybe_get_active). It sets no ability_used flag and has no effect on attacking, so switching another Pokémon in to attack that turn is unaffected. The search filters on Psychic type only, any stage, so Basic or Stage 1 both qualify (shared_mutations.rs:38-49). The card moves straight to hand with no reveal event (shared_mutations.rs:137-175), and the opponent's view masks it (observation.rs:56, 678-683). Test: tests/pokemon/additional_ability_logic_test.rs:168-195 (Natu added to hand at turn start).
result.note: Order: advance_turn queues the normal draw (state/mod.rs:1206), and then the Strange Singing mutation puts its card into hand. The claim says nothing about draw order.

claim: Magneton's Volt Charge Energy is separate from the normal attachment: on T3 Volt Charge gave Magneton 1 Energy and the same player still attached its normal Lightning to Miraidon ex.

It resolves via attach_energy_from_zone(..., is_turn_energy=false) (apply_abilities_action.rs:668-676). attach_energy_from_zone clears energy_zone.current only when is_turn_energy is true (state/energy.rs:26-28), so the normal turn attachment is still offered (move_generation/mod.rs:77-92). result.note: The Magneton tests don't assert that the turn Energy is still there afterward. That part rests on energy.rs:26-28.

claim: Darkrai's Bad Dreams works from the Bench on the turn Darkrai is benched: benched on T2, it dealt 20 to the Asleep opposing Active at the end of that turn (Bulbasaur 60->40).

result.evidence: Bad Dreams maps to BadDreamsEndOfTurn{20} (effect_ability_mechanic_map.rs:734-737). At the end of the owner's turn, on_end_turn calls apply_bad_dreams_damage_for_owner (hooks/core.rs:415), which runs before the Checkup. That function scans every in-play Pokémon of the owner, Bench included, with no played_this_turn gate (hooks/core.rs:619-630). It deals 20 non-attack damage if the opposing Active is Asleep (hooks/core.rs:636-653). Tests: tests/darkrai_bad_dreams_test.rs:134-161 (a Benched Darkrai triggers alongside the Active one) and :12-36 (20 to an Asleep Active).

claim: A Knocked Out Pokemon goes to the discard pile with all its attachments: Exeggutor's Giant Cape, Espurr's 2 and Team Rocket's Rattata's 1 Psychic Energy, and Houndstone's Psychic Energy all left play with it. The owner's Active Spot stays empty until a promotion.

result.evidence: Code: engine/src/state/mod.rs:1252-1264 (discard_from_play). A Knocked Out Pokemon's card, the cards under it and its attached Tools go to its owner's discard pile. Its attached Energy goes to discard_energies, and the board slot is set to None. It is called from the KO wave at engine/src/actions/apply_action_helpers.rs:795. After that, apply_action_helpers.rs:880-886 calls trigger_promotion_or_declare_winner (state/mod.rs:1361-1424), which queues a Promote choice, so the Active Spot stays empty until that choice resolves. Tests: engine/tests/revavroom_tools_test.rs:305-312 (the KO'd holder leaves the Active empty, and both Giant Cape and Rocky Helmet end up in the discard pile: 'the other Tool must follow its holder to discard on knockout'). engine/tests/tool_energy_conservation_test.rs:36-56 (a KO'd Pikachu ex's Energy all goes to discard_energies). engine/tests/video_evidence/flygon_marshadow.rs:151-192 (after the KO the Active is None, Aerodactyl ex is in the discard pile, and only Promote choices are offered).
result.note: Energy is kept in a separate discard_energies list rather than the card discard pile. That is only how the engine stores it and changes no outcome. One exception is Rescue Scarf (state/mod.rs:1237-1250), which returns the Pokemon card to the hand; it doesn't apply to these cards.

claim: KO order is fixed: attack damage, Knock Out, discard, point award (or Shattering Crystal flip and no-point notice), then the opponent promotes. Only then do end-of-turn effects run (Legendary Pulse draw; Soothing Shore healed 20, 180->200), then the Checkup (Poison 100->90; Sand Slammer hit newly promoted Marshadow).

result.evidence: Code: engine/src/actions/apply_action_helpers.rs:659-660: the KO wave waits until the attack's retaliation has resolved. Lines 682-695: the Shattering Crystal coin (a ResolveKnockoutPoints step) is flipped before any points. Lines 711-797: points are awarded, then the Pokemon is discarded. Lines 874-886: the promotion is queued. engine/src/move_generation/mod.rs:44-66: queued choices such as Promote always come before the EndTurn that follows an attack (end_turn_pending is set at apply_action_helpers.rs:1082-1088). EndTurn (apply_action_helpers.rs:87-117) runs on_end_turn first (hooks/core.rs:381-576; Legendary Pulse at 385-394, Soothing Shore at 569 and 607-616), then the Checkup (apply_action_helpers.rs:286-335: Poison at 296-300, then Sand Slammer at 324 and 401-414, then Knock Outs at 326). Tests: engine/tests/video_evidence/flygon_marshadow.rs:146-203 (the 222326 chain: Dragon Pulse KOs Aerodactyl ex for +2, Marshadow is promoted, then EndTurn/Checkup Sand Slammer takes Marshadow 70->60 and the two Bench Pokemon lose 10 each). engine/tests/rules_repair_timing.rs:315-354 (ResolveKnockoutPoints comes before the Promote choices). engine/tests/pokemon/glimmora_point_denial_test.rs:45-80 (Glimmora is always KO'd, and the coin gives both 0 and 1 point). engine/tests/stadiums/soothing_shore_test.rs:25.
result.note: Two small ordering details differ, and neither changes the game. (1) Inside one KO the engine awards points before it discards, and it flips Shattering Crystal while the 0-HP Glimmora is still on the board. The claim has the discard first. Both happen with no player choice in between. (2) Legendary Pulse only queues a DrawCard frame (hooks/core.rs:390-393). The ordinary EndTurn step then runs the Checkup and advance_turn in the same step (apply_action_helpers.rs:110-114 and 150-165; state/mod.rs:1206 queues the next player's draw on top). So the Suicune ex player's draw actually resolves after the Checkup and after the opponent's turn draw. Checkup results don't depend on the hand, so I found no outcome that changes. Soothing Shore heals right away, before the Checkup, as observed.

claim: On T5, Sunny Scorching KO'd Electrode, Rocky Helmet's 20 then KO'd Castform, Destiny Burst still put 70 on the 0-HP Castform, the attacker's point was awarded first and the opponent's second (1-1), then both players promoted.

result.evidence: Test: engine/tests/pokemon/team_rocket_electrode_destiny_burst_test.rs:8-62. In both seats, with a Stadium in play, Castform Sunny Form's Sunny Scorching hits a 20-HP Team Rocket's Electrode holding Rocky Helmet while Castform is at 20 HP. Result: both Actives are empty, points are [1,1], and the turn player is offered Promote first. Code: engine/src/actions/apply_action_helpers.rs:659-660 (Rocky Helmet retaliation resolves before the KO wave). Lines 696-709: on-KO hooks run while the whole wave is still in play, so Destiny Burst (hooks/core.rs:2185-2217) still hits the Castform already at 0 HP. Lines 711-797: points. Lines 874-886: the attacker is sorted first for promotion. rules/09 'Replay follow-up' records the same 225430 segment passing in the replay corpus.
result.note: The order of the two points within the wave is not exactly the same. The engine awards points in seat order (get_knocked_out, apply_action_helpers.rs:922-935), so when the attacker is in seat 0, the defender's point is added first. Both points are added in one step before any win check (lines 829-868), so the visible result (1-1, then the attacker promotes, then the opponent) matches. The award order could only matter for a simultaneous winning point, which is still an open question (rules/05).

claim: A KO by an Ability in the middle of a turn scores at once and the opponent promotes right away, so that turn's attack hits the new Active: Nightmare Aura KO'd Pikachu (score 0 to 1), Oricorio was promoted, and Shadow Bullet hit Oricorio.

result.evidence: Code: engine/src/state/energy.rs:149-170: attaching a Darkness Energy from the Zone to Darkrai ex does 20 to the opponent's Active. energy.rs:113 then calls handle_knockouts right away, which awards the point (apply_action_helpers.rs:733) and queues the opponent's promotion (lines 880-886). Only attacks set end_turn_pending (lines 1082-1088), and queued choices come before free actions (move_generation/mod.rs:44-55). So the opponent promotes, and then the turn player can still attack the new Active. Tests: engine/tests/pokemon/darkrai_ex_test.rs:122-164 (a Nightmare Aura KO queues the opponent's Promote in the middle of the turn). engine/tests/rules_repair_timing.rs:214-237 (after a non-attack Ability KO, the turn stays with the same player on the same turn).
result.note: There is one existing limitation, already flagged in rules/README as 'Low, probable': Nightmare Aura only fires for the once-per-turn manual attachment (energy.rs:156,159). This recording fits if the attach was the manual one, which is likely. Oricorio's Safeguard stops the 30 that Shadow Bullet does to the Active (Hoopa ex is an ex), while its 20 to the Bench still lands (rules/02 §3, same recording 031901). So 'hit Oricorio' should be read as 'targeted Oricorio'. darkrai_ex_test does not check the score; the point comes from the code path cited above.

claim: Poison Checkup damage (10) finished Pokemon left at 10 HP (Mega Lucario ex 10->0, Indeedee ex 10->0), and the Poison knockout of Mega Lucario ex awarded the full +3 points.
support: Pokemon TCG Pocket Battles - Luckycad Xatu.mp4 @ 03:30-03:47 (seen)
Pokemon TCG Pocket Battles - Luckycad Xatu.mp4 @ 15:16-15:28 (seen)

EndTurn's Checkup Poison KOs it, points[0] == 3 and Win(0)). xatu_checkup.rs:284-296 (Luckycad 15:16-15:28: Indeedee ex with Poison and Poison Barb, Life Drain to 10, then the Checkup Poison KOs it for points [2,0]). claim: Discarding your own Pokemon ex through an attack effect (Wild Swing) is not a Knock Out and gives the opponent no points: scores stayed 1-0 and 1-1 until later knockouts changed them.
support: 20260907_220914 @ Part 2, T7 ~72 s; score 1-1 by ~131 s (inferred)

result.evidence: Code: engine/src/actions/apply_action.rs:1215-1244. Wild Swing removes the chosen Benched Water Pokemon through state.discard_from_play (state/mod.rs:1252-1264). That path never calls award_points (state/mod.rs:1212-1215) and never runs the KO wave. The emptied slots are None, not at 0 HP, so the follow-up KO check (apply_action_helpers.rs:1078-1080; get_knocked_out at 922-935) finds nothing. Mega Sharpedo ex counts as a Water Pokemon (eligible_bench_discards, apply_attack_action.rs:6281-6287). Test: engine/tests/pokemon/gyarados_wild_swing_test.rs:60-110 (the chosen Water Pokemon leave play and go to the discard pile; damage is 20 + 40 for each one).

claim: A concession ends the match at once and counts as a win for the other player. 'Your opponent conceded' appeared on T12 with the score at 1-0, with no separate Victory or result banner.

result.evidence: The engine has no concede action and no concede outcome. A search of engine/src for concede, surrender, forfeit and resign finds only a card name ('False Surrender', engine/src/database.rs:47550). GameOutcome has only Win(usize) and Tie (engine/src/state/mod.rs:27-30). The engine sets a winner in only three ways: points and no-Pokemon checks (engine/src/actions/apply_action_helpers.rs:828-868), an empty Bench on promotion (engine/src/state/mod.rs:1385-1389), and the turn-30 tie (engine/src/state/mod.rs:1201-1204). Nothing in actions/types.rs lets a player leave the match.
result.note: The rule itself agrees with rules/01_game_structure.md:93 and :123 (the conceding player loses, whatever the board or points; official in-app Tips). The on-screen detail ('Your opponent conceded' with no separate Victory banner) is about the game's screens, which the engine doesn't model. The simulator never concedes, so this can't come up in simulated games.

claim: When a player's last Pokemon is knocked out with no Bench to promote, the battle ends at once even below 3 points (seen at 1-0 and 1-2). The KO point is still awarded first, then Victory/Defeat appears with no further turn.

result.evidence: In handle_knockouts_with_prior (engine/src/actions/apply_action_helpers.rs:652-886), each KO first awards its points (award_points, line 733) and then discards the Pokemon (line 795). The end-of-game checks come after that, in this order: T2 tie (832-842), 3-point wins (845-855), then 'no Pokemon left in play -> immediately lose (even if points < 3)' (857-868). The function returns before the promotion loop (870-886). Game::play then stops because is_game_over is true (engine/src/game.rs:185-188), so no EndTurn, Checkup or next turn happens. The empty-Bench promotion route does the same (engine/src/state/mod.rs:1385-1389). Test: engine/tests/public_reply_verifier_test.rs:151-161, for both seats. A fixed-damage attack knocks out the defender's only Pokemon from points 0, and the result has winner == Win(actor) and points[actor] == 1, so the point is scored and the game still ends below 3. Also engine/tests/trainers/sophocles_test.rs:54-67 (attack KO of the lone 60-HP Bulbasaur -> Win(0)) and engine/tests/engine/game_api_test.rs:37-56 (first KO of a Bench-less opponent -> Win(0), points >= 1, Active slot empty).
result.note: The two recorded endings fit the engine. 20260921_150630: Hisuian Zoroark ex's Spiteful Illusion knocks out Gyarados (1 point), 1-2, Defeat. 20260908_190031: 1-0, Victory. In both, nobody reaches 3, so only the no-Pokemon check applies. Engine exceptions that don't come up here: if both sides have no Pokemon left, it's a Tie (858-861); if the side losing its last Pokemon took its own 3rd point in the same exchange, it's the rules4 T2 Tie (832-842). Consistent with first-pass R248.

claim: The battle ends at the knockout that gives the third point. No Pokemon Checkup or further turn is logged ('Points 2 > 3' was the last row). The +1 animation (~269s) and the third point marker (~270s) play before the Defeat screen (~273s).

result.evidence: When an attack causes the KO, the attack's damage, effects and retaliation resolve first, then handle_knockouts (engine/src/actions/attack_outcome.rs:197-208). Inside it, award_points runs (apply_action_helpers.rs:733), then the winner is set as soon as exactly one player has 3 or more points (845-855), with an early return that skips promotion ('short-circuit promotion logic', line 828). apply_common_action_suffix still sets end_turn_pending (apply_action_helpers.rs:1087). But Game::play leaves its loop once is_game_over is true (engine/src/game.rs:185-188), so EndTurn is never applied. EndTurn is the only path into Pokemon Checkup (forecast_end_turn -> forecast_pokemon_checkup, apply_action_helpers.rs:47-117) and advance_turn (state/mod.rs:1186). Tests: engine/tests/video_evidence/mega_sableye.rs:137-146 (the Cursed Jewel KO takes points from 1-2 to 1-3; winner Win(1); move_generation_stack empty right after the attack). engine/tests/video_evidence/flygon_marshadow.rs:240-260 (points [2,3], Win(1), no Promote frame even though Dartrix is still on the Bench). engine/src/game.rs:562-579 (a finished game is not changed by settling pending choices).
result.note: The final attacks here (Hisuian Goodra's Heavy Impact, Donphan, Wailord and Dewott attacks) are plain damage attacks, so no after-KO effects affect the ending. 'At the knockout' means after the whole KO wave, any on-KO retaliation pass (815-826) and any point-denial coin (682-694) have resolved. The +1 animation and point marker are screen details. Their order (point scored, then result) matches award_points happening before the winner is set. claim: The results screen's 'Turns played' counts both players' turns: a game that ended on the 10th turn (5 turns each) showed 'Turns played 10'.

result.evidence: The engine's turn_count goes up by one on every player's turn: state/mod.rs:1199-1200 (advance_turn switches current_player, then turn_count += 1). hooks/core.rs:522-523 says so directly: 'Turn 1 is player 0's first turn, turn 2 is player 1's first turn'. Test game.rs:473-513 (test_poison) steps through turn_count 1, 2, 3 one player's turn at a time, and the game ends with turn_count == 5. The 30-turn tie cap uses the same combined counter: state/mod.rs:1201-1203, test state/mod.rs:1693-1705 (test_advance_turn_declares_tie_after_turn_30). A game that ends on the 10th combined turn would have turn_count 10, the same as 'Turns played 10'.
result.note: The engine has no results screen. The match is on the counting convention: both players' turns count.

claim: The Bench holds at most 3 Pokemon: with Hoopa ex, Darkrai ex and Happiny already Benched, a second Absol fetched by Poke Ball had to stay in hand.

result.evidence: The board has 4 slots per player, one Active and three Bench: state/mod.rs:314 (in_play_pokemon: [[Option<PlayedCard>; 4]; 2]) and :554. Basics can be placed only into an empty slot: move_generation/mod.rs:177-186. With the Active and three Bench slots filled, no Place action is generated. Poke Ball P-A 005 is playable whenever the deck is not empty, whatever the Bench holds: move_generation_trainer.rs:561-570. It puts a random Basic into the hand: apply_trainer_action.rs:99-101 calls pokemon_search_outcomes (shared_mutations.rs:16-28), which moves the card to the hand, not the Bench. So a second Absol fetched with a full Bench stays in hand, as observed.
result.note: No test checks Poke Ball with a full Bench specifically. The verdict rests on the code paths above.

claim: Oricorio's Safeguard shows on the board as a blue Ability marker with no Tool square; it is not an attached Tool (an earlier review mistook it for one).

result.evidence: The engine models Safeguard as Oricorio's own passive Ability, not a Tool. effect_ability_mechanic_map.rs:552-553 maps the Safeguard text to AbilityMechanic::PreventAllDamageFromEx, and :1001 maps that to CardEffect::PreventAllDamageFromEx. It is passive and cannot be activated (move_generation_abilities.rs:214; apply_abilities_action.rs:284-285). The damage hook reads it from the defender's Ability (hooks/core.rs:1569, 1596, 1686-1693). Test engine/tests/pokemon/legacy_ability_logic_test.rs:421-436 (test_oricorio_safeguard_prevents_damage_from_ex_attack): a bare A3 066 Oricorio with no Tool attached blocks Mewtwo ex's attack and stays at 70 HP.
result.note: The blue marker is a display detail the engine doesn't model. The rule behind it, that Safeguard is an Ability and not an attached Tool, matches.

claim: Returning a damaged Pokemon to hand clears its damage: Ilima returned Arceus ex at 20 HP, and it was re-Benched the same turn at full 160 HP (Plains-boosted) with no Energy or Tool, then took a fresh Water.

result.evidence: Ilima (apply_trainer_action.rs:174, 1836-1846) offers ReturnPokemonToHand for a damaged Colorless Pokemon. apply_return_pokemon_to_hand (actions/apply_action.rs:1173-1188) takes the PlayedCard off the board, which carries the damage. Only the card itself, plus any cards under it, goes to the hand. Tools go to the discard pile (:1180) and Energy to discard_energies (:1181). Playing it again goes through apply_place_card (apply_action.rs:1090-1099), which calls to_playable_card (hooks/core.rs:90-103): 0 damage, printed HP, no Energy, no Tools. It then calls refresh_hp_bonuses_all, which applies Starting Plains' +20 to Basics (state/mod.rs:607-648). Arceus ex is a Basic with 140 HP, so it comes back at 160. Tests: ilima_test.rs:60-108 shows the returned Pokemon ends up in hand. stadium_test.rs:588-636 (test_starting_plains_applies_to_pokemon_played_after_stadium) shows a Basic placed under Starting Plains gets +20. The fresh Water attachment afterwards is the ordinary per-turn Energy.
result.note: No single test runs Ilima, re-Bench and full HP end to end. The verdict combines the code path with the two tests above.

claim: Enlarging a card to inspect it does not play or select it: Pokemon Communication inspected in hand went back to hand with no effect or failure message, and Gyarados ex inspected during a Communication choice was not committed.

result.evidence: The engine has no card-inspection or zoom step. Actions are committed choices, such as SimpleAction::Play { trainer_card } or picking an entry from move_generation_stack (move_generation/mod.rs:44-55). There is no preview state, so 'inspect without playing' cannot arise in the engine.
result.note: Purely a client UI behaviour. It affects nothing the simulator models.
